assessmentType: documentation and selected source review; no runtime certification

selectionAssessment.policy: This 22 September source-coverage and eligibility snapshot is historical. Product rights, accepted topology, and measured whole-install resources precede weighted coverage. Conductor stock v3.32.4 remains uncleared; Kestra OSS v2.0.3 remains an earlier behavioral baseline. A Kestra/PostgreSQL pair per harness is rejected. The 23 September holistic reassessment selects Temporal with a stable interpreter first for development, Effect second, and Dagu third; none is production-qualified. LangGraph, n8n Community, and distributed Windmill Community remain excluded. All eight technical scores remain visible and unchanged; Dagu and Effect remain unscored in this matrix.
selectionAssessment.a2aPolicy: Pin the protocol version and transport, advertise the supported subset, and test task correlation, continuation, artifacts, cancellation, and restart reconciliation through native integration or a reusable adapter. An adapter cannot invent guarantees absent from the remote service. Native coverage measures integration convenience, not selection eligibility.

langgraph.label: Excluded by decision
langgraph.license: MIT core; separately licensed deployment platform
langgraph.known: The MIT core can run in an independently hosted production application. The packaged production Agent Server requires a license; its dev server is a development/testing path. A configurable concurrency default is not a verified artificial performance cap.
langgraph.condition: Already excluded by the owner because the platform's commercial self-hosting constraints are unacceptable.
langgraph.path: Retain its feature evidence and scores for comparison. A custom host around the MIT library is technically possible, but does not reverse this decision or put LangGraph back on the shortlist.

conductor.label: Stock blocked; source variant conditional
conductor.license: Apache 2.0 core; Orkes is a separate commercial offering
conductor.known: Apache 2.0 covers Conductor core source, but the published v3.32.4 boot JAR includes an Orkes Community-licensed queue dependency whose rights for this product are unresolved. A pinned PostgreSQL-only source variant built and survived a simple workflow/restart without that direct dependency. Reproducible packaging, full notices, S1–S4 factory behavior and an OSS authorization boundary remain open.
conductor.condition: The stock v3.32.4 assembled artifact cannot be selected without explicit rights for the intended use. The source variant cannot be selected until its full package, one-install operation, factory behavior and external authorization boundary are verified.
conductor.path: Keep the source variant as a conditional technical candidate: reproduce its patched build, audit all bundled dependencies/notices, prove one-install packaging and S1–S4 on that exact artifact. Alternatively obtain written rights for the stock package. Protect every direct API and worker path.

windmill.label: Excluded for current product baseline
windmill.license: AGPLv3 source build; additional Community binary terms
windmill.known: Distributed Community can run ordinary production workers but has proprietary product-use restrictions, quotas and paid performance/governance facilities. The AGPL public oss build enables no_auth and resolves requests as an unrestricted administrative identity; it does not supply Community authentication.
windmill.condition: The scored distributed Community baseline is excluded for the current product: its free terms restrict wrapping, selling and managed-service use without agreement.
windmill.path: Retain the Community score for comparison. A separately assessed AGPL source build could reopen Windmill if its obligations, feature set and external authorization/audit design are acceptable and proven. Its need for a gateway alone is not disqualifying; the immediate exclusion is the assessed binary distribution’s product-use restriction. Commercial embedding permission is another route, outside the requested free baseline.
windmill.decisionBasis: Applied production/product-use constraints; distinct from the explicit LangGraph owner decision.

kestra.label: Potential governance blocker
kestra.known: Kestra OSS v2.0.3 passed bounded native restart, contention, publication, Strands harness and A2A/acceptance slices. A host-local macOS arm64 bundle started JDK, PostgreSQL and Kestra with one command. One warm-idle Kestra JVM used about 650 MiB RSS before PostgreSQL and Strands; a separate pair per harness is rejected as the default. Clean-machine installation, total shared-local resources, full distribution notices, direct-API authorization and production lifecycle remain open; granular RBAC/audit are Enterprise/Cloud.
kestra.condition: Blocks a product commitment if final bundle rights, supported clean-machine installation, external publisher/invocation enforcement or an acceptable shared-local whole-install footprint cannot be established. Per-harness Kestra is not the accepted default topology.
kestra.path: Retain reversible Kestra behavior fixtures. Compare one shared locally managed pair serving two harness instances against Dagu and non-development Temporal on the same package/resource protocol; qualify direct-API protection, recovery, clean-machine distribution and notices before any product selection.

temporal.label: Authoring layer must pass evaluation
temporal.license: MIT server; self-hosting does not require Temporal Cloud
temporal.known: MIT self-hosted production server; Cloud is optional. Native workflow definitions are SDK code. A non-development Temporal Server v1.32.0/PostgreSQL/Zigflow v0.15.2 countertrial passed pinned v1/v2 execution and helper restart. A valid new Zigflow definition still required worker refresh; this is an assessed authoring-layer limit, not a Temporal execution-engine limit.
temporal.condition: A blocker if no maintained authoring layer can publish documents with immutable run bindings, permitted execution, and an acceptable bundled operating cost. Zigflow worker refresh is allowed when rollout is automatic and old versions remain available.
temporal.path: Retain Temporal as a conditional challenger. Managed, version-pinned Zigflow worker rollout is now accepted in principle; its automation, retained-version cost, and recovery must be proved. A maintained stable interpreter remains an alternative with owned language/publication cost. Complete Strands/A2A packaging and resource comparison remain open.

n8n.label: Excluded for current product baseline
n8n.license: Sustainable Use License; source-available, not OSI open source
n8n.known: Internal business automation is permitted. The current official FAQ permits customers triggering operator-built workflows, including connecting their accounts, but restricts external users authoring workflow logic through a UI, API, MCP or an agent acting for them. Community also excludes multi-main, sharing/projects, Git environments and external secret-store integration.
n8n.condition: Excluded from the current factory-authoring product shortlist: the assessed free license does not permit external users or their agents to control workflow logic, or grant unrestricted product redistribution.
n8n.path: Keep the technical comparison. Permitted internal/operator-authored use does not satisfy our product requirement. Only suitable commercial rights or a changed product scope would reopen this baseline; a gateway, custom UI or fork does not fix the license restriction.
n8n.decisionBasis: Applied production/product-use constraints; distinct from the explicit LangGraph owner decision.

strands.label: Potential infrastructure blocker
strands.license: Apache 2.0 SDK; hosted AgentCore is optional
strands.known: Strands is the accepted customized harness for capability agents and factory Directors. Core SDK Graph 1.57.0 resumed pinned v1/v2 snapshots after process kills in a bounded trial. The trial-owned publisher supplied immutable definitions. Two unfenced owners resumed the same checkpoint and both executed delivery, showing that SDK snapshots do not provide per-run fencing or effect deduplication.
strands.condition: Using core Strands Graph as the outer runtime is blocked if the owned publisher, version binding, locking and reconciliation become a bespoke workflow engine or cannot preserve the required contract.
strands.path: Price a product-owned approved-definition publisher, immutable binding, fenced per-run lease/CAS, idempotent effects and remote A2A reconciliation before claiming the SDK can serve as the outer factory runtime. The minimal Graph trial excludes full Strands/A2A resource use.

argo.label: Provisional challenger; production proof pending
argo.license: Apache 2.0 workflow controller, server and CLI
argo.known: Native YAML/JSON Workflow and WorkflowTemplate resources run on Kubernetes. The core license permits product use; no vendor production key is identified. Workflow creation can authorize pod creation, so customer definitions require admission policy, restricted identities and isolated execution.
argo.condition: A blocker if operating Kubernetes is unacceptable or if a safe permitted workflow vocabulary, remote-task recovery and immutable version bindings cannot be achieved within the accepted integration budget.
argo.path: Evaluate a private controller/server with Kubernetes RBAC, approved versioned templates, admission policy and network/credential isolation. Use the accepted A2A adapter for remote lifecycle handling. Prove restart recovery, nested director waits, cancellation, definition binding and execution overhead before selection.

currentDirection.scoreRelationship: The 65-feature source-coverage scores are unchanged and do not determine this product judgment.

productionAudit.evidenceLevel: Primary licenses/documentation, pinned artifact/source inspection and bounded 2026-09-22 runtime probes; no production build, load test or complete distributable-bundle license audit.
productionAudit.scope: Production self-hosting and embedding/redistributing the named runtime in an open-source or commercial Exomachina product. API integration alone does not transfer the runtime license to all Exomachina code. Internal use, customer-authored service and redistributed runtime are distinct uses.
productionAudit.rule: BLOCKED refers to the stated edition/use condition, not every possible deployment. A paid agreement is not a free workaround. Rebuilding a platform or silently losing required guarantees is not an acceptable small integration. Unknown or contradictory evidence stays VERIFY, never cleared by score.

langgraph.runtimeClearance: Unrun: exact build and production behavior not certified

strands.ossProduct: Apache 2.0 SDK permits redistribution with license/notice obligations; separately inspect plugins and tools included in the product.

restrictions.title: Stock v3.32.4 server artifact is not cleared for this product
restrictions.scope: Published conductor-server:3.32.4 boot JAR in an Exomachina open-source/commercial factory product
restrictions.fact: The published server POM declares orkes-conductor-queues:2.0.0.rc3 and the boot JAR ZIP directory contains it. Its Orkes Community License Article 3.3 restricts third-party service and competitive-product uses; Exomachina has no established rights for this assembled package.
restrictions.workaround: Obtain explicit rights for the actual use, or use the pinned PostgreSQL-only source variant that built and ran a simple workflow after removing the direct restricted dependency. Reproducible packaging, a full dependency/notice audit and factory behavior remain unproved.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Stock artifact remains blocked; source variant is technically viable but not product-qualified

restrictions.title: Host-local bundle passed; clean-machine distribution remains open
restrictions.scope: Kestra OSS v2.0.3 with JDK 25, PostgreSQL 16.15 and copied macOS arm64 dylibs
restrictions.fact: A one-command copied local bundle restarted a paused run on the trial host without Homebrew runtime load paths. It was 609 MiB including 66 MiB state. Clean-machine portability, installer/update/backup ownership, two-harness helper lifecycle, final notices and shaded isorelax provenance remain unproved.
restrictions.workaround: Build and test a signed distributable on the supported clean machines, close the dependency/NOTICE audit and qualify product helper supervision and resources.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible host-local path observed; product package unproved

restrictions.title: Production storage and coordination must be configured
restrictions.scope: OSS production deployment
restrictions.fact: Default standalone SQLite is for local development. Shared database/queue, distributed locking, persistence and operational configuration are required for production.
restrictions.workaround: Use the documented PostgreSQL or other supported production topology. This is deployment work, not a paid runtime unlock.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Simple PostgreSQL workflow/restart observed on source variant; production topology remains unproved

restrictions.title: Integrated scoped authorization is outside OSS baseline
restrictions.scope: Conductor OSS versus enterprise inbound authorization
restrictions.fact: OSS REST/A2A are open by default. Commercial integrated authorization cannot be credited as an OSS facility.
restrictions.workaround: Private network plus a trusted authorization/publication gateway and actor audit trail; cover direct API and worker paths.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible external boundary; not yet proved

restrictions.title: Native A2A release and remote guarantees need proof
restrictions.scope: Pinned OSS integration modules
restrictions.fact: Current docs describe A2A tasks, but do not certify the selected binary, protocol version, continuation or stale-attempt fencing.
restrictions.workaround: Pin module versions and test a reusable adapter where necessary. An A2A adapter is accepted architecture work.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible integration; unrun on source variant

restrictions.title: Distributed Community cannot be treated as a freely wrappable product runtime
restrictions.scope: Selling, wrapping or offering distributed Community as a managed service
restrictions.fact: Community binary terms prohibit these uses without agreement. Internal organizational use and API calls as-is do not establish a general product-embedding grant.
restrictions.workaround: Obtain rights for the exact use or choose another runtime. An AGPL source build is a distinct candidate and must pass its own feature/auth audit.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: No code-only workaround for these binary license restrictions

restrictions.title: Named public OSS build bypasses per-user authorization
restrictions.scope: Unmodified public oss feature-set build when native scoped identity is required
restrictions.fact: At the recorded source revision, the oss feature includes no_auth. The auth path resolves requests to a synthetic admin/superadmin with unrestricted scopes; public user/password functions are unavailable. The Community build includes private auth code.
restrictions.workaround: A trusted external boundary must own all authorization and actor audit, or a separately implemented auth subsystem is needed. Turning off a feature flag alone is not a proven replacement. Do not transplant proprietary auth code.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: No acceptable drop-in OSS production-auth path established

restrictions.title: Dedicated high-throughput workers and native autoscaling are paid
restrictions.scope: Community versus Enterprise performance facilities
restrictions.fact: Ordinary workers incur per-job startup/cleanup. Dedicated script workers that avoid those starts, native autoscaling and advanced worker management are paid; this is not proof that ordinary Community workers are dev-only.
restrictions.workaround: Benchmark ordinary workers at the required load; add worker capacity or external infrastructure autoscaling. Neither establishes identical low-latency behavior.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible scaling alternative; latency equivalence unproven

restrictions.title: Community has user, workspace, storage and retention quotas
restrictions.scope: Published free self-hosted edition table
restrictions.fact: The table lists 3 workspaces, 50 users, 4 groups, 10 SSO users, 100 app guests per 30 days, 10 GiB workspace object storage and job details retained up to 30 days; Git sync is limited to 2 users. Executions are unlimited; no standard-worker numeric cap is established here.
restrictions.workaround: Use only if the quotas fit, retain required artifacts/evidence in approved external stores, or change edition/runtime. Separate infrastructure does not bypass licensing.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible only where required scale and retention fit

restrictions.title: Global concurrency keys, debouncing and priority are paid
restrictions.scope: Native global scheduler controls
restrictions.fact: Per-flow/script shared concurrency limits, debounce/coalescing and step priority are commercial features, beyond ordinary worker capacity and loop limits.
restrictions.workaround: Use one durable admission mechanism with leases/reconciliation, or accept simpler whole-pool limits if sufficient. A plain in-process semaphore is not an equivalent distributed guarantee.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Substantial integration for equivalent global behavior

restrictions.title: Required approver identity and deployment protection are paid
restrictions.scope: Built-in approval and publication controls
restrictions.fact: Forms, authenticated/group approvers, disabling self-approval and protection rulesets have paid boundaries. Ordinary waits and branches do not establish independent acceptance.
restrictions.workaround: Trusted publisher and independent acceptance service may enforce the requirement if every bypass path is closed.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible domain integration; security proof required

restrictions.title: Free audit availability conflicts across official sources
restrictions.scope: Community history and operator audit
restrictions.fact: Pricing excludes free audit logs; dedicated documentation describes Community audit retention. A full audit rating is not justified until the selected artifact is verified.
restrictions.workaround: Downgrade to partial; inspect the actual build and prove actor-attributed records and export/retention.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Unresolved; no production clearance

restrictions.title: Advanced operational telemetry is edition-gated
restrictions.scope: Native observability facilities
restrictions.fact: Pricing gates Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, queue metrics, instance event webhooks, workspace/schedule error handlers and service-log export. Basic run logs remain distinct.
restrictions.workaround: Use host/database monitoring and supported API reconciliation; prove coverage, retention and failure detection rather than assuming paid telemetry is present.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible partial substitute; completeness unproven

restrictions.title: Restart deployed flows from arbitrary nodes is paid
restrictions.scope: Production recovery versus editor preview
restrictions.fact: Editor preview/reuse and durable execution are distinct from the paid facility to restart a deployed flow from a selected node/version.
restrictions.workaround: Use supported retry/checkpoint recovery where sufficient; bespoke arbitrary replay requires side-effect and version controls.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Limited alternative; not equivalent to arbitrary restart

restrictions.title: Agent evaluation and conversational surfaces are beta
restrictions.scope: Documented beta integrations
restrictions.fact: Beta agent sessions/evals do not establish stable whole-factory supervision, protected evaluation or bounded autoresearch.
restrictions.workaround: Keep these outside required production guarantees until pinned and tested; own the domain-specific evaluator and campaign policy.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Separate domain work; beta status unresolved

restrictions.title: Native granular RBAC and operator audit require Enterprise
restrictions.scope: OSS basic authentication versus operation-level controls
restrictions.fact: Enterprise supplies scoped RBAC, service accounts, richer identity controls and audit logs. OSS basic authentication is not equivalent.
restrictions.workaround: A private engine with a trusted publisher, scoped gateway and external actor audit can satisfy a deliberately bounded deployment.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible external boundary; unrun

restrictions.title: Native worker/tenant isolation and priority pools are paid
restrictions.scope: Multi-tenant and evaluation resource boundaries
restrictions.fact: Enterprise worker groups, isolation and tenant facilities cannot be assumed in OSS. Core flow concurrency is available and must not be marked wholly paid.
restrictions.workaround: Use separately isolated OSS deployments and credentials, network controls and infrastructure reservations. This adds operational units.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible but material infrastructure

restrictions.title: External secret-management facilities are paid extras
restrictions.scope: Native secret-store and secret governance extensions
restrictions.fact: OSS environment-backed secret references satisfy basic secret binding. External vaults, managed secret facilities and fine-grained audit/access add Enterprise requirements.
restrictions.workaround: Inject environment-backed secrets into the intended process with external secret tooling and separation of instances.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Good workaround for basic binding; full external-vault feature absent

restrictions.title: Native unit-test fixtures and promotion facilities are paid
restrictions.scope: Built-in testing, release and incident tooling
restrictions.fact: Enterprise Unit Tests, Promote and Cases do not belong to the free execution engine. Playground and ordinary test flows have narrower contracts.
restrictions.workaround: Use an external fixture runner, version-controlled publisher and incident store. This does not count as native capability or a zero-cost replacement.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible domain/tooling work; effort must be accepted

restrictions.title: Recursive Subflow calls are prohibited
restrictions.scope: Native direct/indirect self-recursion
restrictions.fact: Nested workflows are available; calling a flow recursively through Subflow is prohibited.
restrictions.workaround: Use bounded loops or explicit external nested-factory delegation. Self-recursion is optional here.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Good workaround for current requirements

restrictions.title: Factory documents need a separately assessed authoring layer
restrictions.scope: Document-only authoring requirement
restrictions.fact: The native runtime executes SDK workflow code. An interpreter can accept documents without per-definition code deployment, but Temporal core does not supply the managed factory language/publication platform.
restrictions.workaround: Reuse an existing layer or explicitly own a restricted interpreter. Stock Zigflow v0.15.2 needs worker refresh for new definitions; Tracecat supplies publication but brings platform and license constraints. Local pinning/recovery probes do not resolve this gate.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible paths; publication and ownership gate unresolved

restrictions.title: Product roles and credential policy require application ownership
restrictions.scope: Self-hosted authorization and capability bindings
restrictions.fact: Server authorization extension points and workflow logic exist, but Exomachina roles, publication policy and a credential catalog are not turnkey runtime facilities.
restrictions.workaround: Configure supported authorization and an explicit trusted publisher; keep credential issuance in a separate approved service.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible integration; unrun

restrictions.title: Payload offloading is preview and not an artifact repository
restrictions.scope: Official External Storage versus application artifacts
restrictions.fact: Official payload offloading is preview. Workflow history is not unlimited artifact storage; service limits and retention apply.
restrictions.workaround: Use durable object storage and validated references through Activities, independently of preview payload offloading.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Good artifact-reference workaround; unrun

restrictions.title: Customer-authored factory products lack a free license grant
restrictions.scope: External users controlling workflows / competing product / unrestricted redistribution
restrictions.fact: The current FAQ excludes external users determining workflow logic through UI, API, MCP or an AI agent. SUL also restricts redistribution and competing automation products; publishing source or hiding the editor does not remove the restriction.
restrictions.workaround: Use only permitted internal/operator-authored automation, obtain commercial rights covering the exact product, or choose another engine.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: No code-only or wrapper workaround

restrictions.title: Multi-main availability is paid
restrictions.scope: Production control-plane failover
restrictions.fact: Community queue mode has workers but does not include multi-main availability. Worker scaling is not the same as main-process failover.
restrictions.workaround: Use supervised single-main restart if its downtime and missed-trigger behavior are acceptable. Do not claim equivalent zero-downtime multi-main.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Limited workaround; not equivalent when HA main is mandatory

restrictions.title: Sharing, projects, SSO and source-control environments are paid
restrictions.scope: Native collaboration and release governance
restrictions.fact: Community excludes project/workflow/credential sharing and source-control environments; advanced identity and review facilities are also paid.
restrictions.workaround: Use private instances, a trusted publisher and independently enforced credentials and identities. Separate instances increase operations.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible constrained deployment; not native collaboration parity

restrictions.title: External vault and external binary storage are paid extras
restrictions.scope: Basic credential references versus enterprise storage integrations
restrictions.fact: Community supports encrypted credential references and appropriate filesystem/database binary storage, but external secret-store and external binary-storage integrations are paid.
restrictions.workaround: Use supported core storage, or application-owned object storage through permitted nodes with explicit authorization and retention.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Good basic-binding alternative; storage recovery must be tested

restrictions.title: Native log streaming is paid
restrictions.scope: Execution polling versus full lifecycle audit delivery
restrictions.fact: Community has ordinary logging and execution records; full log-streaming integrations require a paid edition.
restrictions.workaround: Poll supported APIs and retain an external authenticated audit trail where needed; validate gaps and event ordering.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible partial substitute; not full streaming parity

restrictions.title: Queued work does not prove interrupted-node recovery
restrictions.scope: Failure during active remote work
restrictions.fact: Persisted waits, node progress and queues do not establish automatic continuation of every interrupted action or discovery of an accepted remote submission after a lost response.
restrictions.workaround: Persist intent and task identity, reconcile remote work and stop on unresolved effects. Test actual crash points.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible adapter; actual guarantees unrun

restrictions.title: Packaged production Agent Server requires a license
restrictions.scope: Using the vendor production server without commercial entitlement
restrictions.fact: Official CLI requires a production license key for up; standalone servers require license verification. MIT graph-library rights do not include that packaged platform entitlement.
restrictions.workaround: Pay for the platform or build a separate host around the MIT core. The latter is substantial platform work and does not reverse the user exclusion.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: No acceptable free packaged-production workaround established

restrictions.title: Development server is not the production architecture
restrictions.scope: langgraph dev rather than a custom MIT-library host
restrictions.fact: The dev path uses local/in-memory persistence and targets development/testing. Configurable worker concurrency defaults are not a verified licensing throttle.
restrictions.workaround: A real custom production host needs durable persistence, scheduling, concurrency/ownership and operations, or use the licensed server.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Not an acceptable drop-in production workaround

restrictions.title: SDK does not include a managed outer factory platform
restrictions.scope: Production hosting of factory graph workflows
restrictions.fact: The Apache SDK is usable in production without a vendor license, but publication, execution hosting and operational control are application responsibilities.
restrictions.workaround: Use it inside A2A services or explicitly own the missing host and publication system.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Substantial platform work if selected as outer runtime

restrictions.title: Session persistence has no distributed writer lock
restrictions.scope: Multiple processes operating the same graph/session
restrictions.fact: Session management does not provide distributed locking; competing writers can overwrite state. Recovery checkpoints do not establish attempt ownership.
restrictions.workaround: Use a single authoritative owner with durable leases and fencing, or an external execution engine.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Substantial ownership/recovery work; unrun

restrictions.title: Enterprise workers depend on valid licensing
restrictions.scope: Enterprise worker runtime, distinct from Community
restrictions.fact: Pinned worker code stops accepting work when the license is invalid. Offline rights and renewal behavior cannot be inferred from the AGPL core or public stub code.
restrictions.workaround: Use a licensed deployment whose exact offline/expiry terms are acceptable, or evaluate a permitted free distribution.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: No free substitute for proprietary runtime entitlement

restrictions.title: NSJAIL production entitlement conflicts across docs/source
restrictions.scope: NSJAIL isolation in a non-enterprise build
restrictions.fact: Source labels NSJAIL an Enterprise feature available for testing; broader isolation docs do not state that boundary consistently. Ordinary container/PID isolation is a separate mechanism.
restrictions.workaround: Do not count NSJAIL as cleared free production isolation. Prove a container/VM/PID alternative against the required threat and credential boundaries.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Narrower alternatives exist; NSJAIL entitlement unresolved

restrictions.title: Non-enterprise email trigger has a daily cap
restrictions.scope: Built-in email-trigger parent jobs
restrictions.fact: Pinned worker code caps non-enterprise parent email-trigger jobs at 100 per day. This is distinct from the general unlimited-executions claim.
restrictions.workaround: A separate permitted mail receiver can invoke ordinary API/webhook flows, or use an appropriate licensed edition.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible connector alternative; verify delivery/idempotency

restrictions.title: Native secured worker-controller transport is Enterprise
restrictions.scope: Current 2.0 distributed worker transport
restrictions.fact: Current architecture docs describe plaintext OSS gRPC; native TLS, mTLS and JWT worker authentication are Enterprise features. Private addressing alone is not authenticated encrypted transport.
restrictions.workaround: Operate an independently authenticated encrypted tunnel/mesh or isolated trusted deployment, then prove both identity and traffic protection.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible external transport; material configuration and validation

restrictions.title: Native versioned plugins and alternate queue backends are paid
restrictions.scope: Plugin dependency versions and scaling backend choice
restrictions.fact: Enterprise adds per-plugin versioning and alternative backend choices. OSS database-backed HA is available; it must not be mislabeled Enterprise-only.
restrictions.workaround: Pin complete worker images/dependency sets and use supported JDBC production storage.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Good bounded deployment alternative; per-run dependency isolation needs proof

restrictions.title: Telemetry and purge policy need explicit configuration
restrictions.scope: OSS network independence and retained evidence
restrictions.fact: Server and UI telemetry have separate default-on switches; purge flows govern retained executions/logs. No license-imposed OSS retention or worker-count cap was found.
restrictions.workaround: Disable unwanted telemetry with documented configuration and define backups/purge policy. EE keys and user/service-account limits are separate.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Good supported configuration path

restrictions.title: Payload/history/fan-out have technical limits
restrictions.scope: Self-hosted defaults, not paid capacity tiers
restrictions.fact: Documented defaults include 2 MB payloads, 50 MB/51,200-event histories and 2,000 pending activities/children/signals/cancel requests. Some thresholds are configurable; large histories and unbounded fan-out still need design limits.
restrictions.workaround: Use object references, bounded fan-out and Continue-As-New where applicable; tune supported limits only after load testing.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Good architectural/configuration paths; no payment unlock

restrictions.title: Concurrency knobs do not cover every execution type
restrictions.scope: Regular mode, queue workers and evaluation runs
restrictions.fact: Regular self-hosted production has no default concurrency cap; its optional limiter excludes manual, subworkflow, error and CLI executions. Queue concurrency defaults to 10 per worker and is configurable, not a worker-count license cap.
restrictions.workaround: Size worker pools and enforce admission across all relevant entry paths. Do not claim a single setting bounds all factory work.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible admission design; scope must be proved

restrictions.title: Definition-history retention has a docs/code conflict
restrictions.scope: Workflow versions, distinct from execution logs
restrictions.fact: Docs describe unlimited definition retention via -1, while the active source helper clamps it to a license limit with a 24-hour unlicensed default. Do not promise unlimited Community history without a pinned-release check. Execution pruning separately defaults to 336 hours/10,000 records and is configurable.
restrictions.workaround: Retain approved immutable definitions and required execution evidence independently; verify exact release retention and recovery semantics.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible external archive; native history limit unresolved

restrictions.title: Native metric evaluations cover only one Registered Community workflow
restrictions.scope: Evaluation availability, not merely run concurrency
restrictions.fact: Registered Community enables native metric evaluation for one workflow; broader self-hosted availability is Enterprise. The default single concurrent evaluation can be overridden by a documented setting, but that does not remove feature-availability restrictions.
restrictions.workaround: Use an independent evaluator/test runner with a protected dataset and results store, or appropriate licensing.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible domain evaluator; not native multi-workflow eval parity

restrictions.title: Some free tooling requires registration
restrictions.scope: Registered Community extras
restrictions.fact: Debug-in-editor, folders and custom execution metadata require optional free registration/email/key; base Community runtime does not.
restrictions.workaround: Use base pinning/manual tests without registration, or accept the registration requirement.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Good basic-testing alternative; exact tooling differs

restrictions.title: Licensed features add renewal and execution-metering dependency
restrictions.scope: Paid self-hosted features, not the base Community runtime
restrictions.fact: Paid self-hosted plans ordinarily renew through the license server and meter production executions. Licensed features can deactivate if renewal fails; vendor-issued air-gap certificates are a separate route. Community telemetry/update/template calls can be disabled.
restrictions.workaround: Stay within permitted Community use or obtain a contract/certificate whose offline, usage and expiry behavior meet the deployment requirements.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: No code-only substitute for paid entitlement; offline terms need verification

restrictions.title: Agent Server package has separate managed-service restrictions
restrictions.scope: langgraph-api 0.14.3 and commercial deployment components
restrictions.fact: The publisher identifies langgraph-api 0.14.3 as Elastic License 2.0, with hosted/managed-service and license-key restrictions. The MIT core license does not grant these components equivalent embedding rights.
restrictions.workaround: Use only the MIT library in independently owned infrastructure, obtain suitable vendor terms, or retain the current exclusion.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: No license-key bypass or repackaging workaround

restrictions.title: Standalone server deployment has operational constraints
restrictions.scope: Licensed standalone Agent Server
restrictions.fact: Production documentation identifies Kubernetes as the maintained deployment path, requires license verification/usage reporting and warns standalone scale-to-zero can lose tasks.
restrictions.workaround: Use the supported paid topology and explicit drain/availability policy if reconsidered; currently excluded.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: No free platform workaround established

restrictions.title: Orkes Developer Edition is not the OSS production distribution
restrictions.scope: Optional Orkes commercial deployment, not Conductor OSS
restrictions.fact: Free Orkes Developer Edition is an experimentation environment. Current on-prem image instructions require paid entitlement and an authorization token. OSS licensing does not establish commercial Orkes redistribution or offline rights.
restrictions.workaround: Use the documented Conductor OSS production topology, or obtain a commercial contract specifying production, embedding, capacity, renewal and offline rights.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Good free OSS runtime alternative; commercial entitlements remain separate

restrictions.title: Kubernetes is the execution control plane
restrictions.scope: Self-hosted Argo Workflows OSS
restrictions.fact: Workflow state, scheduling and pod execution depend on Kubernetes. Production HA requires resource allocation, controller leader-election/rollout configuration and a healthy Kubernetes API; this is not an edition restriction.
restrictions.workaround: Operate the documented Kubernetes topology, artifact repository and optional SQL persistence. If Kubernetes operation is unacceptable, Argo is an architectural mismatch.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible deployment path; infrastructure responsibility and load/recovery proof remain

restrictions.title: Customer authors need a controlled publication boundary
restrictions.scope: Untrusted authors of Workflow and WorkflowTemplate resources
restrictions.fact: Workflow creation can cause the controller to create arbitrary pods and use namespace service accounts. Strict/Secure restrictions constrain submitted Workflows, but approved-template authoring and allowed entrypoint overrides still need governance.
restrictions.workaround: Give customers restricted authoring/publication APIs; enforce approved templates, service accounts and public entrypoints through admission controls and RBAC. Separate controller, candidate and evaluator namespaces; apply pod/network policy.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible bounded admission and cluster-policy integration; bypass resistance unproved

restrictions.title: Authentication mode must preserve caller authorization
restrictions.scope: Server/client/SSO authentication configuration
restrictions.fact: Client mode uses caller Kubernetes permissions. Server mode uses the server service account; SSO also needs explicit SSO RBAC to map users to scoped service accounts. Login alone does not establish tenant isolation.
restrictions.workaround: Choose client authorization or configure and test SSO RBAC mappings. Retain distinct caller audit evidence and prevent broad server-account access from bypassing the publication boundary.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Native configuration path; deployment-specific proof pending

restrictions.title: Name references require immutable publication discipline
restrictions.scope: Template references, active runs and rollout
restrictions.fact: TemplateRef has no version/digest field. Referenced templates are cached when resolved, so unvisited references may resolve changed names. Secure restriction errors on underlying template changes rather than providing transparent version isolation.
restrictions.workaround: Publish dependencies under immutable versioned names, prohibit mutation/deletion while referenced, pin container images and environment bindings, and record the complete dependency set. Test updates during waiting runs.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible publication contract; stricter than mutable template updates and unrun

restrictions.title: Remote A2A lifecycle and external-effect safety remain integrations
restrictions.scope: Opaque external services and custom HTTP/plugin tasks
restrictions.fact: HTTP/plugin execution is not native A2A. Persisted engine state, retry nodes and locks do not atomically record an external effect or establish remote stale-attempt fencing after an ambiguous reply.
restrictions.workaround: Use a reusable protocol adapter with durable task correlation, service-supported idempotency/status lookup, scoped cancellation and fenced result acceptance. Preserve unknown outcomes when the service cannot prove success or non-execution.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible adapter only where remote contracts support it; no universal exactly-once workaround

restrictions.title: Artifact prefixes are not an access-control boundary
restrictions.scope: Shared artifact repository credentials and tenant data
restrictions.fact: Artifact repository documentation explicitly permits keys containing parent-directory traversal. Directory-like prefixes alone do not isolate tenants or protect evaluator data; authority follows the credentials supplied to workflows.
restrictions.workaround: Enforce least-privilege storage IAM and credential separation, restrict artifact repository overrides and validate references. Protect evaluator objects from candidate credentials independently of workflow path conventions.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible storage-policy integration; tenant access tests pending

restrictions.title: Workflow state is bounded by Kubernetes resource size
restrictions.scope: Large graphs, fan-out and node histories
restrictions.fact: Workflow resources face the documented roughly 1 MB object limit. Node compression and SQL offloading mitigate status growth, but do not make arbitrarily large workflow specifications valid.
restrictions.workaround: Configure SQL node offloading where needed, reuse templates and split large compositions. Load-test expected fan-out, output sizes and Kubernetes API throughput.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Documented scaling options; structural limits remain and workload capacity is unrun

restrictions.title: Execution archive, logs and operator audit are separate
restrictions.scope: Production history and audit retention
restrictions.fact: The optional SQL archive stores completed workflow status and outcomes, not pod logs. Kubernetes Events can be lost or aggregated; creator labels are not a complete record of operator actions.
restrictions.workaround: Configure SQL retention, external log/artifact retention and Kubernetes/API actor auditing; capture evidence before workflow or artifact garbage collection. Reconcile authoritative workflow state rather than driving automation from Kubernetes Events.
restrictions.workaroundQuality: Feasible deployment and audit integration; retention/restore proof pending

restrictions.scope: Exact production build and enabled Argo features
restrictions.fact: Assessment combines current documentation with inspected source snapshot 8a6f33f90a2124878db858e04c6999d3c5ab63b2. No pinned production release, controller-failover test, hostile-author test or dependency-license audit was executed.

productionAudit.selectionPolicy: Eligibility and accepted topology precede weighted coverage and operational judgment. LangGraph is excluded by owner decision; n8n Community and distributed Windmill Community remain excluded for the assessed customer-authored product use. Conductor stock v3.32.4 is not cleared because of a restricted bundled dependency; its PostgreSQL-only source variant is unqualified. Kestra v2.0.3 is the observed behavioral development baseline, but a separate Kestra/PostgreSQL pair per harness is rejected as the default. A shared local helper remains conditional on whole-install resources, lifecycle, distribution and authorization. Bounded Dagu, non-development Temporal and core Strands Graph countertrials have run: Dagu is a light declarative challenger with transitive child-pinning work; Zigflow still requires worker refresh; core Strands Graph requires fenced same-run ownership after duplicate fixture delivery. Their full product gates remain open. All eight technical options remain selectable in the comparison; UI selection does not grant product eligibility.

candidateScreening.title: Dagu: focused production and factory-composition screen
candidateScreening.baseline: Unmodified Dagu Community self-hosted server and workers, used through the CLI/HTTP boundary; no paid controls or proprietary embedded Go API license assumed.
candidateScreening.evidenceLevel: Primary documentation and source inspection. No runtime, concurrency, recovery, security, or legal-distribution certification. No feature-matrix score assigned.
candidateScreening.releaseCaveat: Current documentation and repository main can precede a released binary. Pin a release and confirm every relied-on capability before the spike.
candidateScreening.summary: Dagu Community v2.17.0 ran as a lightweight file-backed local helper and preserved native nested approval through restart. A paused parent invoked a changed child definition after resume, so transitive immutable publication is required. GPL-compliant packaging, product authorization, independent-root lifecycle and real A2A recovery remain open.

freeProduction.finding: Community is offered for continuing self-hosted use with unlimited servers and workers. No developer-only restriction or documented license execution-count cap was identified. Retention and capacity still require deployment configuration.

ossDistribution.finding: GPL-3.0-or-later permits commercial activity and GPL-compliant redistribution. Distributing Dagu requires the applicable notices and corresponding-source obligations; an OSS label alone does not establish compatibility for a combined work.

commercialProduct.finding: A separately operated CLI/server is materially different from importing Dagu into a distributed Go binary. GPL does not automatically cover every independent HTTP client. A proprietary combined binary that cannot comply with GPL needs separate embedding rights. A self-host plan is not evidence of those rights.

strengths.finding: Native YAML and MCP read/change/execute tools provide a credible agent authoring loop: inspect, preview/apply definitions, then explicitly start or enqueue. Exomachina still supplies publication policy and capability contracts.
Distributed workers, queues, retry scanning, and persistent run snapshots provide existing execution infrastructure. Separate factory services need not invent another DAG scheduler.

restrictions.finding: The public source license is GPL-3.0-or-later. Proprietary distribution that links the experimental Go API raises combined-work obligations; the vendor offers separately negotiated non-GPL embedding rights.
restrictions.condition: Blocking only if our chosen distribution forms an incompatible combined work and we require neither GPL compliance nor a separate agreement.
restrictions.response: Evaluate a separate server/HTTP packaging model and its actual notices/source delivery. Do not infer that a container boundary settles every licensing question. Commercial customer-authored workflows are not themselves prohibited by GPL.

restrictions.finding: Community supports the first administrator and up to two API keys. Additional user management, OIDC/SSO, audit logs, and incident routing are paid controls. Workspace roles are explicitly not tenant isolation.
restrictions.response: A private runtime behind Exomachina-owned authentication, authorization, audit, and per-tenant deployment boundaries is feasible engineering. It must not expose an unrestricted engine credential to customers. This does not make native Community RBAC or audit complete.

restrictions.finding: With no configured license, source enters Community mode without activation. Key-based paid activation uses periodic heartbeats; signed inline/file JWT sources do not. License startup failures degrade rather than block application startup.
restrictions.response: Do not describe Community as requiring registration or payment. If paid controls are chosen, establish supported offline entitlement and failure behavior for those controls. This inspection does not certify absence of every unrelated outbound request.

restrictions.finding: The processless typed action human.task is allowed only in roots, not DAGs invoked by dag.run, dag.enqueue, or parallel. It also rejects foreach placement and step timeout settings.
restrictions.response: Evaluate independent root services for reusable factories. Do not generalize this restriction to every approval gate: current source has sub-DAG approval/resume endpoints, while approval inputs differ from typed human-task outputs.

restrictions.finding: Automatic DAG retries require the scheduler, explicit retry policy, and an eligible failed top-level run. The default scan window is 24 hours from the original run timestamp, so long-lived runs can age out.
restrictions.response: Configure the recovery window for factory lifetimes and define escalation beyond it. Worker-crash tests in source demonstrate failure detection paths, not verified exactly-once external effects or complete Exomachina recovery.

restrictions.finding: HTTP-started roots are not automatically a native parent/child execution tree. Dagu can own each root's execution while Exomachina owns the logical service relationship.
restrictions.response: Persist versioned invocation identity, parent/child linkage, deadline and budget authority, cancellation state, accepted results, and recovery ownership. A one-shot callback or in-memory map is insufficient.

restrictions.finding: Distributed transport documents TLS/mTLS, but peer.insecure defaults to true. Web/API TLS is a separate concern. No paid-only transport gate was identified in the reviewed Dagu documentation.
restrictions.response: Configure and test authenticated encrypted transport plus private API access. Do not equate available TLS with a hardened default installation.

separateRootComposition.answer: Yes, provisionally: expose every reusable factory as an independent root run behind an HTTP service, optionally with an A2A facade. Each root may then own processless waits. Dagu's scheduler still owns queueing and execution; Exomachina needs a durable service-coordination adapter, not a replacement DAG scheduler.
nativeMechanisms: HTTP APIs start/enqueue roots, accept supplied run IDs, inspect state, stop runs, and expose completion/resume operations.
A human task persists Waiting and releases its attempt. Completion commits validated input before enqueueing a continuation of the same run from its stored snapshot.

Repeated identical completion is documented as idempotent; queue failure after persistence can be repaired through resume/repeated completion. These semantics do not establish idempotent external agent submission.
proposedFlow: Publish an immutable factory revision and persist an invocation intent with stable logical action ID, run ID, caller, contract, deadline, and budget reservation.
Submit the callee as a root through the service adapter. If acceptance is uncertain, reconcile by identity before starting another invocation.
Let the caller reach a dedicated result checkpoint. Let the callee independently run, pause for decisions, and resume through Dagu.
Persist the callee's accepted terminal outcome. An authenticated reconciler completes the caller's checkpoint with a compact result reference and outcome.
Use scheduled reconciliation to recover lost callbacks, delayed queueing, cancellation, deadlines, and abandoned ownership. Its persistent records must survive process failure.
adapterResponsibilities: Correlation: stable factory revision, contract and execution profile, logical invocation ID, caller/callee run and attempt identities, and artifact references.
Delivery races: a result can arrive before the parent checkpoint exists; retain and retry delivery rather than discard an early callback.
Cancellation: propagate cancellation across roots, reconcile already accepted remote work, and reject late results after authority is revoked.
Deadlines: propagate an absolute deadline and enforce expiry while runs are waiting. A synchronous HTTP request timeout is not cancellation; the documented start-sync timeout leaves the run active.
Budgets: reserve and reconcile shared token, cost, concurrency, and depth limits across independent roots; prevent fan-out from independently spending the same remaining budget.
Recovery: an elected/fenced owner reconciles unresolved submissions and callbacks before creating new effects; recovery of the adapter itself cannot depend on a lost in-memory task.
Publication: bind a logical factory version to the exact submitted definition/dependencies. A stored run snapshot does not by itself provide a complete authorized, immutable factory catalog.
separateRootComposition.alternativeToTestFirst: For a simpler post-execution review, test native sub-DAG approval/resume before adding separate roots solely to emulate a human task. Typed form semantics, worker release, restart behavior, and distributed propagation still need proof.
separateRootComposition.notEstablished: No native A2A factory facade, atomic concurrent root-submission deduplication, automatic cross-root cancellation/budget cascade, or production-safe bridge is claimed. No no-feasible-workaround blocker has been established for the HTTP composition route.

proofObligations.title: Pin a distributable production baseline
proofObligations.scenario: Build/deploy the chosen released artifact without registration or a paid key; document separate-service versus combined-binary packaging.
proofObligations.passCriteria: Required capabilities exist in that release; GPL notices/source delivery and product license boundaries are resolved; no trial expiry governs the Community runtime.

proofObligations.title: Both roots wait across complete host loss
proofObligations.scenario: Caller and callee independently reach durable checkpoints; kill server/scheduler/workers, replace workers, edit the source definitions, then complete the waits.
proofObligations.passCriteria: Waits free execution capacity, persist through restart, resume the intended snapshots, and produce one accepted downstream effect.

proofObligations.title: Lost acceptance and duplicate submissions
proofObligations.scenario: Drop the child-start response after acceptance and concurrently retry the same logical invocation from two recovery processes.
proofObligations.passCriteria: One logical child and one external effect; existing execution is recovered rather than duplicated. Run-ID prechecks alone are not accepted as concurrency proof.

proofObligations.title: Early, duplicated, stale, and partially committed results
proofObligations.scenario: Deliver a child result before the caller checkpoint, duplicate it, lose the resume response, and fail queueing after completion was persisted.
proofObligations.passCriteria: Durable reconciliation eventually resumes once; incompatible or revoked results cannot overwrite accepted state; no completed input is lost.

proofObligations.title: Cancel and expire a waiting tree
proofObligations.scenario: Cancel/expire the caller while the child is running or waiting, including a race with result delivery and recovery-owner replacement.
proofObligations.passCriteria: Cancellation/deadline policy reaches every correlated root and remote assignment; no late callback resurrects authority or permits a new effect.

proofObligations.title: Concurrent budgets and isolation
proofObligations.scenario: Fan out competing independent roots under one budget, then crash the reservation owner; attempt cross-customer API and artifact access.
proofObligations.passCriteria: Atomic reservations cap aggregate use, recovery reconciles outstanding spend, and the Exomachina gateway/deployment boundary enforces tenant access despite shared engine credentials.

proofObligations.title: Long-lived failure recovery and worker leases
proofObligations.scenario: Kill workers during a remote side effect, test coordinator replacement, and fail a run older than the configured automatic-retry window.
proofObligations.passCriteria: One fenced recovery owner reconciles effects before replay; failure beyond the window is escalated or explicitly recovered without silent abandonment.

proofObligations.title: Compare native sub-DAG approval with root-service composition
proofObligations.scenario: Run a nested approval gate locally and on distributed workers; approve, reject, restart, and lose a response.
proofObligations.passCriteria: Determine which requirements native approval meets, including release of waiting capacity and parent continuation; add an adapter only for the remaining typed-wait/service semantics.

candidateScreening.recommendation: Keep Dagu as a credible unscored lightweight challenger. Run the complete Strands+A2A product slice and serial matched resource comparison only after its exact GPL bundle, Community authorization boundary, transitive definition binding and independent-root recovery approach are accepted. Do not infer whole-install memory from this partial topology.
candidateScreening.userFacingAssessment: Dagu now has a pinned local trial: one warm helper used 120.8 MiB RSS and nested approval survived restart. A child edited while its parent waited ran the new version after resume, so publication must pin children. The package is promising but has unproved product rights, authorization and A2A recovery.

importanceLegend.most: Decisive for the architecture or a critical operating guarantee. Prove this before production.
importanceLegend.mid: Important to effective operation or improvement. Depth and native tooling can follow the core path.
importanceLegend.least: Lower selection priority. Can be deferred or handled through a simpler path for the initial factory.

importanceBasis: Exomachina architecture requirements; separate from engine support and Baseline/Next/Optional requirement status. Lower importance does not waive a required control.

scoring.scope: All 65 features, including Baseline, Next and Optional; importance supplies the only requirement weight. Filters and column selection do not change the ranking.
scoring.formula: 100 × Σ(importance weight × support credit) / Σ(importance weight)
scoring.tieBreak: Most weighted coverage, then Mid weighted coverage, then alphabetical display order; exact score ties are not meaningful preferences.
scoring.weightedTopFourPool: Assessed outer runtimes not excluded for the current product. Strands is a worker SDK/component, so it remains in overall coverage but outside this pool.
scoring.sectionScope: Each section score covers all features in that section, normalized by its own available weighted points. Search and Baseline-only filters hide rows without changing scores. Overall coverage is calculated from total earned points, not an unweighted average of section percentages.
scoring.eligibilityRule: Eligibility and operational judgment are separate from coverage. Conductor is assessed as a conditional PostgreSQL-only source variant; its stock artifact is uncleared. Kestra is the provisional development baseline, Temporal a direct conditional candidate and Argo provisional. Excluded baselines and Strands remain visible; Dagu is unscored.

conductor.baseline: Self-hosted Conductor OSS with documented free integration modules enabled. Current official documentation assessed 2026-09-21; no release pinned or runtime conformance tested. Enterprise-only capabilities are partial, not baseline support.

native_definition.note: Canonical JSON is stored, versioned and executed by the engine; SDK authoring produces the same native definition document.

publish_no_deploy.note: New definitions reuse existing workers and built-in tasks; registering another composition does not require redeploying those implementations.

schema_discovery.note: Published JSON Schemas describe workflow, task and runtime objects; metadata APIs expose registered task and workflow definitions.

validate_only.note: The workflow validation endpoint checks a candidate definition without saving it and returns structured invalid-definition error details.

agent_authoring.note: Official CLI and REST operations support authoring, validation, registration and execution; external agents can operate these documented interfaces.

version_binding.note: Active executions retain their starting definition snapshot through updates; recorded snapshots also govern ordinary retries and restarts.

dependency_bundle.note: Definitions and task metadata are exportable, but assembling worker artifacts, integrations and environment compatibility remains deployment integration work.

branch.note: Native task sequences and SWITCH operators route using workflow inputs or structured task outputs through explicit configured branches.

parallel_join.note: Fork and JOIN operators express parallel task dependencies; optional-task and failure settings specify which failures may be tolerated.

dynamic_map.note: Dynamic forks create runtime-selected per-item work and JOIN collects results; task-definition concurrency limits cap execution of worker tasks.

bounded_loop.note: DO_WHILE conditions can bound iterations and route exhaustion; configured workflow and task timeouts provide additional explicit execution limits.

advanced_join.note: EXCLUSIVE_JOIN supplies first-completion behavior, but acceptance predicates, quorum accounting and reconciliation of surplus remote work need additional orchestration.

nested.note: SUB_WORKFLOW specifies child name, version and mapped inputs; its outputs and execution identity are available to the parent.

recursive.note: Dynamic child-workflow invocation supplies composition primitives; a depth counter and shared recursion budget must be enforced in the definition.

typed_io.note: Runtime schemas exist, but externalized task outputs and asynchronous system-task outputs bypass checks; missing registry documents can silently disable enforcement.

mapping.note: Task input parameters and workflow output expressions explicitly select upstream fields, structured values or artifact references for each boundary.

lineage.note: Execution records preserve task references, iterations and outputs; semantic item identities and artifact transformation lineage require explicit metadata.

a2a_client.note: Native AGENT, GET_AGENT_CARD and CANCEL_AGENT tasks handle supported A2A calls; protocol compatibility still requires checking the selected release.

a2a_expose.note: Workflow-backed A2A endpoints expose Agent Cards, task status and artifacts; enabling integration and configuring access control remain deployment requirements.

remote_reconcile.note: Polling mode persists remote task IDs, deadlines and failure counts; restart resumes polling, and push notifications have a polling backstop.

attempts.note: Task references, iteration identity, task execution IDs and retry history distinguish the logical workflow step from its separately recorded attempts.

external_dedupe.note: Stable message IDs support correlation, but no native cross-service atomic ledger prevents arbitrary concurrent external effects after ambiguous replies; receiving services must enforce idempotency.

artifacts.note: Configured external payload storage keeps large workflow and task inputs/outputs outside execution records and exposes retrievable storage references.

artifact_acceptance.note: The native model stores task results and payload references; revision-specific acceptance and repair invalidation require a separate domain model.

durable.note: Persisted workflow/task state and at-least-once delivery support recovery after failure; effects inside workers must tolerate repeated delivery.

preserve_success.note: Task retry and failed-work recovery use recorded execution state; already completed sibling work need not be rerun with the failed task.

retries.note: Task definitions configure bounded backoff retries; terminal-error statuses distinguish nonretryable failures from failures eligible for another configured execution attempt.

timeouts.note: Task response, task execution and workflow timeouts have configured outcomes; native A2A additionally supports an absolute call deadline.

waits.note: WAIT and HUMAN persist time-based or external-signal gates in execution state, permitting later completion through documented APIs or events.

commands.note: Task-update APIs address a particular running task and accept decision outputs; validating domain payloads and decision authority requires additional checks.

cancel.note: Subworkflow termination and explicit remote CANCEL_AGENT provide cancellation primitives; remote outcomes and detached child policies still require reconciliation.

unknown.note: Persisted A2A IDs aid reconnects, but no universal uncertain-action protocol resolves a lost acceptance response before the remote ID is recorded.

compensation.note: A failureWorkflow can inspect completed actions and execute explicitly authored compensations; application services implement each actual undo operation.

triggers.note: REST starts, event handlers and the optional native scheduler launch executions; required event-broker and scheduler modules must be configured.

catchup.note: The scheduler can replay missed cron slots or advance from current time; catch-up bursts require capacity-aware and idempotent downstream services.

overlap.note: The scheduler explicitly lacks an overlap-policy field; a new scheduled run may start while the prior execution remains active.

capacity.note: Task concurrentExecLimit bounds in-flight tasks across polling workers and leaves excess work queued until capacity is released. This supplies task processing capacity; unified whole-factory admission and remote spending reservations remain separate integration.

priority.note: Workflow start priority and task-domain capacity lanes prioritize work; end-to-end fairness across competing factories is not established by those controls.

ownership.note: The engine ignores completion after task timeout. Fencing competing still-active worker deliveries needs release-specific proof; this rating concerns result commitment, not external effects.

budget.note: Time, turn, token or execution quotas are not an attributed monetary-spend ledger with budget admission across remote services; that capability requires integration.

eligibility.note: Engine task eligibility follows workflow state; cancellation or reassignment in an external work system needs a dedicated synchronization authority.

rbac.note: OSS REST and A2A are open by default; scoped integrated authentication is enterprise functionality, otherwise an external gateway must enforce access.

secrets.note: Credential injection and per-call headers are documented, but verify OSS secret-provider coverage; secure environment binding may live in workers or gateways.

isolation.note: Invocation context and credential bindings scope supplied data; enforcing tool and data permissions inside opaque remote agents remains their responsibility.

gates.note: Native waits and branches enforce configured paths, but reviewer independence and required acceptance policy are application-level constraints requiring validation.

stale_decisions.note: Task completion targets a task ID; artifact-revision comparison and stale approval rejection are not represented by the native human-task contract.

policy_validation.note: Structural and runtime schema validation are native; approved service identities, immutable review gates and publication permissions require domain-specific policy checks.

learning.note: Versioning and test APIs support deliberate updates; automatically converting execution feedback into governed factory improvements requires a separate authoring capability.

visual_graph.note: The stored executable definition has UI parity, and execution inspection exposes actual task states alongside the workflow graph structure.

history.note: Execution and task histories support operational diagnosis; authenticated operator audit evidence needs configured identity and auditing beyond the open OSS API baseline.

events.note: The PostgreSQL-only source variant retains explicit EVENT tasks and execution APIs, but removes the workflow-event-listener module that publishes automatic lifecycle status to Kafka, queues or webhooks. Add a separate publisher for equivalent automatic events.

pinned_debug.note: Mock-output tests substitute results by task reference and iteration; a persistent interactive pin-and-run visual workflow is not the documented interface.

testing.note: The workflow test API supplies task outputs and simulated timing, tests branches and nested workflows, and returns a simulated execution.

fork.note: Retry, restart and task rerun use recorded definitions; explicit restart on latest is supported and can repeat external side effects.

work_management.note: Workflow metadata and decision gates do not provide a goal/owner work-management layer spanning executions; Exomachina must supply that domain capability.

conversation.note: A2A input-required continuation can resume waiting workflows through messages; broader conversational supervision and command authorization require an application interface.

incident_cases.note: Correlation IDs and failure workflows identify related executions; they do not supply a shared incident-case lifecycle or atomic symptom coalescing.

recovery_playbooks.note: Failure workflows and guarded tool execution support repair paths; approved playbook contracts, repair-specific authority and post-repair verification need application integration.

trace_regressions.note: Agent SDK record/replay and eval assertions reuse sanitized traces; a revision-linked fixture catalog and opaque A2A boundary evidence remain application responsibilities.

protected_evaluator.note: Tool and command allowlists constrain supported agents; immutable evaluator assets and candidate workspace permissions require separately enforced storage and execution boundaries.

candidate_comparison.note: Agent eval suites provide trace assertions and optional model judges; paired factory baselines, pinned fixture provenance and promotion rationale require integration.

scoped_learning_memory.note: Persisted agent state is execution memory; contract-scoped procedural lessons, rejected-change reasons and obsolete-guidance invalidation require a separate domain model.

staged_rollout.note: Versioned workflow definitions preserve execution bindings; selecting candidate cohorts and restoring traffic to a previous version requires caller-side release routing.

research_isolation.note: Isolation groups separate HTTP/Kafka queues and thread pools; execution namespaces separate executors, while research credentials and reserved production capacity need deployment controls.

proactive_research.note: Documented bounded agent loops and evals are building blocks; they do not implement an opt-in experiment campaign, trial ledger or promotion lifecycle.
