native_definition.note: Native YAML declares tasks, inputs, outputs and orchestration; the server stores and runs flow definitions without generating orchestration application code.

publish_no_deploy.note: New YAML compositions can be deployed through CLI/API using installed plugins; no worker deployment is required for rearranging existing primitives.

schema_discovery.note: The documentation MCP exposes plugin schemas, options and versions; live instance schemas help authors match the actual available task catalog.

validate_only.note: The supported CLI validates candidate flow files before deployment and returns errors without replacing a published flow definition.

agent_authoring.note: External-agent skills combine live schemas with CLI validation, deployment and execution; documentation MCP itself supplies context rather than running flows.

version_binding.note: Every flow change creates a revision and drafts stay unpublished; child references can pin revisions instead of selecting the latest.

dependency_bundle.note: YAML and namespace files are portable components; dependency/environment checks require deployment tooling, with richer packaging and promotion features in Enterprise.

branch.note: Sequential, If, Switch and DAG primitives route structured outputs through explicit configured conditions and dependencies without an LLM choosing every transition.

parallel_join.note: Parallel and DAG tasks express required dependencies and completion; AllowFailure and configured error behavior govern tolerated branch failures.

dynamic_map.note: Loop expands a runtime collection into per-item work, supports concurrency limits and makes iteration outputs available for downstream aggregation.

bounded_loop.note: LoopUntil accepts maximum iterations and duration; configure failOnMaxReached or explicit routing because reaching limits otherwise defaults to successful completion.

advanced_join.note: The documented core flow vocabulary supplies Parallel/Dag completion joins, not an acceptance-aware race or quorum operator with surplus-work reconciliation.

nested.note: Subflow binds namespace, flow ID and optional revision, maps inputs/outputs, and configures waiting and propagation of child failure.

recursive.note: The subflow contract explicitly prohibits direct and indirect recursive calls; bounded iteration must use loop primitives instead of cyclic subflow invocation.

typed_io.note: Inputs support typed and JSON-schema validation; arbitrary remote result and intermediate output contracts need explicit validation steps beyond declared output fields.

mapping.note: Expressions select task outputs and file URIs, while explicit flow outputs define the public results passed to parent workflows.

lineage.note: Task-run identities and stored output references preserve execution provenance; semantic item mapping and artifact-revision lineage need additional domain metadata.

a2a_client.note: The free AI plugin provides a native A2A prompt proxy; its documented contract exposes text output rather than comprehensive task lifecycle controls.

a2a_expose.note: The A2A plugin is a client; native callable flow exposure uses MCP, so an Agent Card and A2A task server need an adapter.

remote_reconcile.note: The A2A proxy returns text without a durable remote-task handle; worker resubmission alone cannot reconnect and reconcile the original remote task.

attempts.note: A task run retains its identity and attempt history; retries create new attempts while replay can create a separately linked execution.

external_dedupe.note: Worker resubmission is at least once. Preventing concurrent duplicate external actions after ambiguous replies requires the receiving service’s idempotency and reconciliation contract.

artifacts.note: Internal storage persists task files and exposes URI references for downstream tasks, inspection and retrieval outside transient worker memory.

artifact_acceptance.note: Output fields and stored files have no native acceptance-revision lifecycle; invalidating prior acceptance after repair requires a separate application model.

durable.note: Persisted execution state and server heartbeats drive failure recovery and job resubmission; workers must tolerate the documented at-least-once behavior.

preserve_success.note: Task retries and restart target failed work in the existing execution; explicit replay creates a new execution and can reuse prior outputs.

retries.note: Bounded constant, exponential and random retry policies are native; selective failure classification depends on the task/plugin or explicitly authored routing.

timeouts.note: Runnable task attempt timeouts, overall retry duration and loop duration bounds constrain execution; configured flow handling determines the exhaustion response.

waits.note: Persisted Pause and Sleep tasks model external decisions or timers; executions can resume later through the UI or API.

commands.note: Paused executions can receive correlated resume inputs through UI/API; broader command validation and state-dependent authority need additional application policy.

cancel.note: Execution kill supports child propagation control, but completion of cancellation inside opaque remote services remains dependent on their integrations.

unknown.note: Execution state and error routing are available; a native uncertain-action reconciliation protocol for arbitrary remote services is not provided.

compensation.note: Authored error/finalization tasks and subflows can perform explicit recovery actions; application implementations determine whether those effects are actually reversible.

triggers.note: API calls, schedules, webhooks, flow-state changes and plugin event triggers start executions through native supported integration surfaces.

catchup.note: Schedule recovery explicitly chooses ALL, LAST or NONE for missed slots, with a maximum accepted lateness option and backfill support.

overlap.note: Trigger concurrency and flow queue/cancel/fail controls exist; current pages disagree on skipped versus queued blocked triggers, so pin and verify behavior.

capacity.note: Flow concurrency limits queue excess executions, while Parallel/Loop limits bound task expansion; namespace-wide and tenant-wide controls have edition considerations.

priority.note: Enterprise worker queues provide reserved-capacity priority lanes; equivalent documented fairness controls are outside the OSS baseline selected for this comparison.

ownership.note: Worker job ownership and heartbeat recovery coordinate attempts. The exact rejection of obsolete result commits after reassignment needs verification against a pinned release.

budget.note: Time, turn, token or execution quotas are not an attributed monetary-spend ledger with budget admission across remote services; that capability requires integration.

eligibility.note: Triggers evaluate start conditions, but continuous authority over canceled or reassigned external work items requires a separate reconciliation capability.

rbac.note: Scoped RBAC, service accounts and richer authentication are Enterprise features; OSS basic authentication does not supply equivalent operation-level authorization.

secrets.note: OSS secret() resolves environment-backed references outside flow YAML; dedicated secret storage, fine-grained access control and audit are Enterprise capabilities.

isolation.note: Selected inputs and Enterprise isolation constrain local execution, but invocation-specific permissions across opaque remote services require service-side enforcement and bindings.

gates.note: Pause/approval and branching implement review steps; proving independent reviewers and enforcing non-bypassable acceptance across publications needs domain policy.

stale_decisions.note: Resume addresses an execution, but the approval contract does not bind acceptance to immutable artifact revisions or automatically reject stale decisions.

policy_validation.note: Enterprise policies can validate and enforce flow/plugin configuration; catalog identity, review independence and acceptance invariants still need Exomachina-specific checks.

learning.note: Authoring skills and revisions facilitate intentional changes; a feedback-driven, tested and governed factory-improvement loop is a separate application capability.

visual_graph.note: The UI presents executable flow structure and execution state, including topology, task status, logs and outputs for inspection.

history.note: Task attempts, errors and execution histories are native; comprehensive authenticated operator audit logs are an Enterprise feature beyond the OSS baseline.

events.note: Execution APIs and flow-state triggers expose lifecycle transitions; plugin triggers and outputs supply programmatic progress integration for configured systems.

pinned_debug.note: OSS Playground reuses earlier outputs while rerunning downstream tasks, but requires upstream execution; supplied fixture substitution is a separate Enterprise testing feature.

testing.note: The native fixture-and-assertion workflow Unit Tests feature is Enterprise; OSS can execute test flows but lacks that same declarative harness.

fork.note: Replay starts a new execution from a selected task and links the original; prior outputs may be reused, so inspect side-effect boundaries.

work_management.note: Enterprise Cases add incident ownership, response targets and remediation tracking; general factory goals and authority across executions remain application-level concepts.

conversation.note: MCP flow invocation and paused-run resume inputs provide useful primitives; a conversation continuously supervising authoritative run commands requires an application layer.

incident_cases.note: Enterprise Cases link related failed executions and track resolution; documented matching is non-atomic, so concurrent failures can still create duplicate cases.

recovery_playbooks.note: Error handlers and Enterprise Case actions invoke repair flows; scoped operational permissions exist commercially, while playbook preconditions and verification remain authored logic.

trace_regressions.note: Execution replay supplies historical context and Enterprise unit tests accept fixtures; sanitization, trace-to-fixture promotion and revision-linked evidence need integration.

protected_evaluator.note: Enterprise worker isolation and governance restrict runtime access; separating immutable evaluator assets from editable candidate resources still requires deliberate deployment and permission design.

candidate_comparison.note: Enterprise unit tests provide fixtures and assertions, but no native paired quality/cost comparison with uncertainty and keep/reject evidence is established by this test interface.

scoped_learning_memory.note: Flow revisions and key-value storage retain data; they do not model validated state-local guidance, rejected edits or contract-aware lesson invalidation.

staged_rollout.note: Enterprise Promote copies published revisions between environments with review and audit; cohort routing and coordinated rollback remain external release-process responsibilities.

research_isolation.note: Enterprise worker groups and worker isolation provide dedicated execution boundaries; separating production credentials, quotas and experiment permissions requires configured deployment policy.

proactive_research.note: Flows, schedules and agent tasks orchestrate work, but an objective-bound experiment campaign with trial decisions and autonomous stop policy requires application implementation.

validate_only.note: Argo lint validates workflows and referenced templates, including strict checks and offline bundles; submission also supports server dry-run validation.

agent_authoring.note: Supported CLI, Kubernetes and REST APIs let external agents validate, create and submit workflow definitions; no native MCP authoring server is assumed.

version_binding.note: Runs retain specifications and resolved templates; unresolved references resolve by name. Immutable version-named dependencies need publication enforcement; Secure mode errors on template changes.

dependency_bundle.note: Offline lint can resolve templates supplied together; portable container images, secrets, artifact stores and environment compatibility still require deployment-level packaging and checks.

branch.note: Sequential steps, DAG dependencies, when conditions and expression tags route execution using explicit task outputs and structured JSON expressions.

parallel_join.note: DAG dependency edges and parallel steps wait for required predecessors; failFast controls whether independent branches continue after a failure.

dynamic_map.note: withParam expands runtime JSON arrays into task instances, aggregates outputs, and combines with template parallelism or synchronization to bound concurrency.

bounded_loop.note: Finite loops and recursive templates with explicit counter conditions express bounded repair; workflow/template deadlines provide additional enforced termination limits.

advanced_join.note: Dependency expressions support task-result predicates and AnySucceeded/AllFailed aggregates; acceptance-aware quorum selection and cancellation of surplus remote work require orchestration logic.

nested.note: Reusable templates expose parameters and artifacts, but templateRef names carry no immutable version field; versioned resource names and publication restrictions must establish bindings.

recursive.note: Templates can invoke themselves recursively. Depth counters, shared budget propagation and authorization bounds must be explicitly implemented in the approved composition.

typed_io.note: Required parameters and enum values receive validation, but parameter/result values are not generally checked against capability JSON Schemas; reusable validators remain necessary.

mapping.note: Named parameters, artifact references and expression mappings pass selected inputs and outputs through tasks, loops and nested templates.

lineage.note: Persisted node identities, relationships and outputs expose execution provenance; immutable artifact revisions and lineage across repairs require application identifiers and records.

a2a_client.note: HTTP templates and executor plugins provide integration points, not native Agent Card discovery or A2A task semantics; a reusable protocol adapter is required.

a2a_expose.note: Workflow submission and status APIs do not supply an Agent Card or A2A endpoint; a separate service must translate the protocol.

remote_reconcile.note: Durable node outputs can retain remote IDs and subsequent HTTP tasks can poll them; an adapter must resolve ambiguous dispatch and reconnect semantics.

attempts.note: Workflow and node identities, retry-node relationships, timestamps and outputs persist separately, retaining logical task context alongside recorded retry attempts.

external_dedupe.note: Concurrency locks and output memoization do not transactionally couple dispatch with external effects; duplicate suppression across ambiguous replies requires the remote operation contract.

artifacts.note: Configured artifact repositories persist task inputs and outputs outside pods, with retrievable storage references and credential bindings propagated through the workflow.

artifact_acceptance.note: Artifact references and suspend approvals carry data, but there is no native acceptance ledger that invalidates approvals when an artifact revision changes.

durable.note: Workflow state persists in Kubernetes; replacement controllers resume reconciliation, while configured retries recover failed pods and SQL offloading supports larger node histories.

preserve_success.note: Retry resumes failed workflows without repeating successful nodes by default; memoized resubmission can also reuse recorded successes in a new execution.

retries.note: Per-template retryStrategy supports failure classifications, expressions, limits and backoff, with last-attempt status, exit code and duration available to conditions.

timeouts.note: Workflow and template activeDeadlineSeconds enforce execution deadlines; resulting terminal statuses can drive explicit failure handling and recovery paths.

waits.note: Suspend templates persist waiting state until a duration elapses or an authorized resume/input command arrives; controller replacement retains workflow state.

commands.note: CLI and APIs target named workflows and selected nodes, supplying declared intermediate outputs and resuming suspended execution under Kubernetes authorization.

cancel.note: Stop runs exit handlers and terminate skips them; independently created child workflows and opaque remote tasks need explicit cancellation propagation and outcome reconciliation.

unknown.note: Native node phases describe engine execution, not an unresolved remote side effect; timeout/error states do not provide a protocol-level unknown-outcome reconciliation ledger.

compensation.note: Exit handlers and result-conditioned recovery templates run application-defined cleanup or reversal steps; authors define which external effects can actually be compensated.

triggers.note: REST/CLI submissions, authenticated event bindings and CronWorkflows start executions; event queue delivery and admission limits require ordinary operational configuration.

catchup.note: CronWorkflows configure missed-start grace with startingDeadlineSeconds; automatic recovery schedules one eligible missed instance, with documented backfill patterns for broader catch-up.

overlap.note: Cron concurrency policies allow, forbid or replace overlaps; workflow mutexes and semaphores provide queued admission for shared execution scopes.

capacity.note: Controller, namespace, workflow and template parallelism plus mutexes/semaphores bound concurrency and queue excess work; shared database locks can coordinate multiple controllers.

priority.note: Queued workflows use explicit numeric priority, then creation-time ordering for locks; namespace limits and multi-lock blocking constrain achievable dispatch fairness.

ownership.note: Leader election and persisted node/task-result identities coordinate engine ownership; stale external completions need explicit fencing, with end-to-end attempt authorization still unproved.

budget.note: Resource-duration statistics estimate requested compute usage, not attributed model/service spend; native concurrency and deadlines do not implement monetary budget admission.

eligibility.note: RBAC authorizes API operations and pod identities; the controller does not continuously interpret external assignment ownership or revoke remote work when eligibility changes.

rbac.note: Kubernetes resource verbs and namespace roles separate template management, workflow submission and operation; optional SSO maps users/groups to scoped service accounts.

secrets.note: Kubernetes Secret references bind environment variables, mounted files and artifact credentials without placing secret values in workflow documents.

isolation.note: Namespaces, workflow service accounts and network/storage policies supply isolation primitives; remote capability scopes require adapters, and unrestricted authors can select namespace service accounts.

gates.note: Dependencies and suspend inputs express approval paths; author restrictions and independent publication authority must additionally prevent bypass and enforce reviewer independence.

stale_decisions.note: Scoped node commands resume a selected wait but do not inherently compare an approval with the current artifact revision or superseded acceptance state.

policy_validation.note: Strict/Secure template restrictions and structural validation constrain submissions; approved capability identities, bounded domain loops and non-bypassable acceptance paths need additional admission policy.

learning.note: Execution archives and reusable workflows provide evidence and execution primitives, but no native continuous engineering loop proposes, evaluates and governs improved factory versions.

visual_graph.note: The workflow UI displays declared dependencies and live node outcomes, backed by the same persisted workflow resources that drive execution.

history.note: Workflow status and SQL archives retain outcomes, nodes and attempts; logs need separate retention, and creator labels do not provide a complete operator audit.

events.note: API/CLI watches and persisted workflow progress expose lifecycle state programmatically; Kubernetes Events are lossy notifications and must not be treated as durable automation history.

pinned_debug.note: Debug pause inspects live containers, and memoization reuses outputs; these are not an interactive visual facility for substituting pinned downstream test examples.

testing.note: Lint checks definitions and memoization reuses outputs, but the assessed authoring tools provide no workflow test harness for scripted task-result and failure injection.

fork.note: Resubmit creates a new workflow, optionally reusing successful nodes with memoized execution; retries can target nodes, while rerun tasks may repeat external effects.

work_management.note: Workflow metadata and creator labels describe executions; accountable goals, assignment ownership and escalation authority above runs require a separate work-management model.

conversation.note: The native supervision surface is UI/CLI/API commands; conversation identity and authorized interpretation into run commands require a separate product integration.

incident_cases.note: Workflow archives and notifications record run failures, but there is no native cross-run incident fingerprint, concurrent case coalescing or case-ownership lifecycle.

recovery_playbooks.note: Reusable templates, scoped RBAC and exit handlers can execute repair playbooks; version immutability, preconditions, verification and distinct repair/publication authority need domain policy.

trace_regressions.note: Archived runs and memoized resubmission preserve source examples; sanitization, revision-linked expected outcomes and conversion into reusable regression fixtures require an engineering integration.

protected_evaluator.note: Kubernetes RBAC and restricted templates can isolate evaluator resources; approved publication and namespace/storage policy must keep candidate authors from mutating protected evaluation assets.

candidate_comparison.note: Parallel DAGs and retained outputs can run experiments, but no native paired evaluator tracks comparable quality, cost, uncertainty and keep/reject decisions.

scoped_learning_memory.note: Archived workflow records are execution evidence, not a version-aware store of rejected changes, validated lessons and their contract/policy applicability.

staged_rollout.note: Version-named templates and scoped submission support controlled candidates, but cohort routing, rollback records and immutable dependency enforcement require a publication/admission layer.

research_isolation.note: Separate namespaces, service accounts, pod scheduling and concurrency pools can isolate evaluation; reserved production capacity and storage/remote credential boundaries need enforced cluster policy.

proactive_research.note: Schedules, loops and deadlines can execute trials, but no native research campaign model enforces hypothesis scope, spend, allowed edits and a keep/reject ledger.

bounded_loop.note: Ordinary deterministic loops enforce explicit iteration limits and escalation outcomes; Continue-As-New can bound history for lengthy repeated processes.

mapping.note: Workflow code explicitly selects and transforms Activity results into subsequent arguments, including object-store references instead of entire artifacts.

lineage.note: History relates Activity inputs, outputs and execution events; semantic artifact ancestry through aggregation and repair requires application identifiers.

a2a_expose.note: Workflow and Nexus endpoints do not natively publish A2A Agent Cards or implement A2A task endpoints for arbitrary Workflows.

remote_reconcile.note: Durable history, heartbeats and asynchronous Activity completion retain correlation primitives; remote task discovery and reconciliation require a service-specific adapter.

attempts.note: Workflow, Run and Activity identities distinguish logical execution and retries; Activity attempt metadata and retry history support correlation.

external_dedupe.note: Workflow-start identity prevents duplicate workflow starts, not duplicate Activity effects. Concurrent external-action deduplication and ambiguous-reply reconciliation require the participating service.

artifacts.note: Durable payloads support references; official External Storage offloads large payloads but remains Public Preview and needs an operator-managed store.

artifact_acceptance.note: History preserves payloads, but artifact revision acceptance and automatic downstream invalidation are domain concepts without a native implementation.

durable.note: Event History replay restores Workflow progress after Worker failure; persistence preserves scheduled tasks and completed Activity results across service restarts.

preserve_success.note: Replay uses recorded completed Activity results; retrying a failed Activity does not re-execute successfully recorded sibling Activities.

retries.note: Activity Retry Policies define attempt limits, intervals, exponential backoff and non-retryable error classifications with SDK failure handling.

timeouts.note: Workflow and Activity timeout types bound total execution, individual attempts and heartbeat gaps; failures can trigger explicit recovery paths.

waits.note: Durable timers and Signal or Update handlers persist waiting state without requiring a continuously running Worker process or conversation.

commands.note: Workflow handles address particular executions; Updates support validation, acceptance tracking and returned results, while Signals provide durable asynchronous input.

cancel.note: Parent Close Policy and SDK cancellation modes control native child workflows. Cancellation acceptance and actual completion inside opaque remote services still require integration and reconciliation.

unknown.note: History and timeouts preserve evidence, but an explicit uncertain-action reconciliation protocol for arbitrary external effects remains application functionality.

compensation.note: Documented Saga patterns execute explicit compensating Activities under durable Workflow control; application code supplies each effect-specific compensation.

triggers.note: SDK and API clients start Workflows, event handlers can invoke those clients, and native Schedules start recurring executions.

catchup.note: Schedules define a catchup window, explicit backfill and pause-on-failure behavior, preserving deliberate handling of starts missed during service downtime.

overlap.note: Schedule overlap policies include skip, buffer-one, buffer-all, allow-all, cancel-other and terminate-other, providing explicit behavior for overlapping scheduled work.

capacity.note: Worker slots, concurrency settings and Task Queue dispatch throttling bound processing capacity while excess Workflow and Activity Tasks remain queued.

priority.note: Self-hosted Task Queues support priority levels and configurable weighted fairness; ordering is approximate across queue partitions, not a global strict sequence.

ownership.note: Service-managed Activity task tokens and execution state reject obsolete completion attempts; external side effects still require their own fencing.

budget.note: No native cross-service spending ledger or budget admission controller; recording usage in Workflow state would be application functionality.

eligibility.note: Signals, Updates and cancellation accept intervention commands; detecting and continuously reconciling external work ownership and authorization requires an application authority.

rbac.note: Self-hosted JWT claims and Authorizer plugins enforce API permissions; product-specific author, publisher and operator separation needs configured or custom authorization.

secrets.note: Activities can use environment credentials and payload encryption; there is no built-in factory credential-binding catalog or secret-management service.

isolation.note: Namespaces, authorization and encrypted payloads provide isolation primitives; per-assignment remote data and tool permissions require service enforcement.

gates.note: Durable conditions and decision handlers enforce coded gates, while reviewer independence and globally non-bypassable publication rules require application policy.

stale_decisions.note: Update validators can reject mismatched current state before acceptance; artifact revision checks and decision freshness remain application-specific conditions.

policy_validation.note: No native factory publication policy checker validates capability identities, budgets and required review paths before deploying arbitrary Workflow code.

learning.note: SDK tests and code versioning are available, but converting run feedback into governed factory improvements is not a built-in lifecycle.

visual_graph.note: The Web UI shows histories, timelines and execution state, but arbitrary SDK control flow has no native declared executable factory graph view.

history.note: Event History records durable execution decisions, results and failures; Web UI and CLI expose histories and recorded operational commands.

events.note: History APIs, CLI following, Queries and SDK observability expose lifecycle and progress; application-specific progress is published through declared handlers.

pinned_debug.note: SDK test doubles and replay exist, but there is no native visual canvas with pinned per-step examples and interactive partial tests.

testing.note: Official SDK test environments support Activity substitutes, failure injection, time skipping and historical replay without deploying production Workers.

fork.note: Workflow reset starts a new run from a selected history point; later Activities may execute again and require side-effect safeguards.

work_management.note: Workflow identities and search metadata do not provide a native goal, accountable-owner and escalation work-management layer above executions.

conversation.note: Signals, Updates and Queries supply authoritative supervision commands; a conversational interface and its intent-to-command authorization remain application integration.

incident_cases.note: Workflow identity and event histories track executions; a cross-run incident-case model with symptom fingerprints, accountable ownership and resolution requires an application.

recovery_playbooks.note: Durable recovery workflows, compensation and API authorization provide primitives; approved repair contracts, narrow action privileges and outcome verification require application policy.

trace_regressions.note: SDK replay tests reuse execution histories to detect incompatible workflow changes; sanitized semantic fixtures and external-agent outcome assertions require separate engineering evidence.

protected_evaluator.note: Separate worker pools and configured API authorization provide boundaries; repository, evaluator and dataset mutation permissions must be enforced outside Workflow code.

candidate_comparison.note: SDK tests and history replay check workflow behavior and compatibility; they do not implement paired quality/cost experiments or evidence-based keep/reject evaluation.

scoped_learning_memory.note: Durable histories and Workflow state retain execution facts; reusable procedural lessons with applicability, rejected-change evidence and invalidation need a separate application model.

staged_rollout.note: Full for native Worker Deployments: percentage ramping, pinned executions and explicit rollback. Retain prior workers; quality decisions and arbitrary remote-agent routing remain application responsibilities.

research_isolation.note: Task queues route separate worker pools and authorization scopes namespace access; resource reservations, external credentials and production/research infrastructure isolation remain deployment responsibilities.

proactive_research.note: Durable workflows can host a research implementation, but campaign hypotheses, mutation scopes, experiment decisions and independent trial/total stop rules are application features.

native_definition.note: Native workflow JSON describes nodes, connections and settings; imported definitions execute using installed node implementations without separate orchestration application code.

publish_no_deploy.note: Saving and publishing a workflow activates a composition of existing nodes; only new node implementations require installation or deployment.

schema_discovery.note: Built-in MCP node search and type retrieval expose exact parameter structures; node configuration validation checks generated schemas before composition.

validate_only.note: MCP validate_workflow returns errors and warnings before creation; validate_node_config separately checks individual parameter schemas without publishing a workflow.

agent_authoring.note: Instance MCP supports discovery, validation, creation, editing, testing and publication for authorized external clients on self-hosted installations.

version_binding.note: Draft and published graph versions are distinct, and saved executions retain original workflow data; settings and referenced dependencies are not fully frozen.

dependency_bundle.note: Preview packages include workflows and dependencies with preflight checks; secrets remain environment bindings, and some packaged resources require paid licenses.

branch.note: If and Switch nodes route structured items through explicit conditions; connected ordinary nodes define sequential transformations and actions.

parallel_join.note: Merge supports joining branch data, but ordinary branches execute sequentially; truly concurrent sub-executions need additional coordination and explicit failure collection.

dynamic_map.note: Item processing and per-item subworkflows handle runtime-sized inputs; bounded concurrent fan-out with aggregation requires additional coordination beyond ordinary sequential branches.

bounded_loop.note: Loop Over Items and conditional back-edges express repeated processing; explicit counters and conditions bound review loops and choose escalation outcomes.

advanced_join.note: Merge is a data-combination primitive; there is no native quorum or first-acceptable completion join that cancels surplus remote work.

nested.note: Subworkflows expose typed input fields and parent-child execution links, but the invocation node does not provide an explicit immutable version selector.

recursive.note: Subworkflow calls and conditional guards permit bounded composition, but recursion depth and shared budget enforcement require explicit workflow state and checks.

typed_io.note: Subworkflow inputs can declare names and types; universal runtime validation of every step and factory output schema is not automatic.

mapping.note: Expressions and the visual mapper select prior node fields into downstream parameters, including identifiers and artifact references through branches.

lineage.note: Native item links trace outputs to inputs through splits and merges. Artifact-revision ancestry and repair lineage need explicit application metadata.

a2a_client.note: The built-in integration baseline does not document a native A2A task client; HTTP requests alone do not implement A2A lifecycle semantics.

a2a_expose.note: Webhook and MCP exposure do not supply A2A Agent Cards or task lifecycle endpoints; an A2A server would be additional integration.

remote_reconcile.note: Persisted execution data and Wait callbacks can retain remote identifiers; recovering and reconciling a live remote agent task needs custom workflow logic.

attempts.note: Execution IDs, retry links and node execution data provide correlation; stable logical assignments spanning remote attempts require an application data model.

external_dedupe.note: Execution queues and retries do not supply a cross-service atomic action ledger; concurrent external deduplication and ambiguous-reply reconciliation require the receiving service.

artifacts.note: Configured filesystem persistence in regular mode or database storage in queue mode retains binary artifacts by reference; choose storage mode and retention deliberately.

artifact_acceptance.note: Execution records and approvals do not natively bind acceptance to artifact revisions or invalidate downstream acceptance after repair.

durable.note: Saved node progress, queued jobs and persisted Wait states support recovery; arbitrary active work and remote effects still need explicit reconciliation.

preserve_success.note: Saving execution progress records per-node data and allows resuming after errors; node retries operate on the failed node rather than completed predecessors.

retries.note: Nodes provide Retry On Fail and error outputs; classified backoff policies require explicit routing, waits or integration-specific behavior.

timeouts.note: Workflow timeout settings cancel executions after configured durations; Wait deadlines and node-specific request timeouts bound external interactions where supported.

waits.note: Wait persists longer timers, webhook callbacks and form waits; time waits shorter than 65 seconds remain in-process and lack the same restart durability.

commands.note: Execution-specific resume URLs correlate authenticated decisions, but arbitrary live-run commands and domain validation require dedicated workflow handlers.

cancel.note: Executions can be canceled and subworkflows can be awaited; no comprehensive parent-close policy matrix reconciles cancellation of independent remote child work.

unknown.note: Saved execution state and error branches do not provide a native uncertain-action reconciliation protocol; remote outcome discovery requires service-specific integration.

compensation.note: Authored error outputs and reusable error workflows can execute explicit compensating actions; application logic supplies effect-specific undo steps and their order.

triggers.note: Webhook, application-event and Schedule Trigger nodes start published workflows; APIs and MCP can also invoke eligible workflows directly.

catchup.note: Opt-in durable scheduler from 2.36 provides grace periods and skip or latest-missed catch-up policies; it does not replay every missed occurrence.

overlap.note: Production concurrency limits queue excess starts, but per-factory skip, coalesce and replacement policies require explicit coordination beyond global FIFO control.

capacity.note: Production limits and queue-worker concurrency bound processing; manual, subworkflow, error and CLI executions have documented exclusions from regular-mode limits.

priority.note: Documented execution queues use FIFO and worker concurrency; configurable business priority and weighted fair dispatch are not native Community controls.

ownership.note: Queue and scheduler claims coordinate local ownership. General rejection of obsolete node-result commits after recovery needs verification; remote-effect fencing is a separate contract.

budget.note: Node counts and execution quotas do not provide a general per-factory external-agent spending ledger with atomic budget admission.

eligibility.note: Triggers and callbacks can report changes, but the baseline has no native continuous reconciliation of external work ownership, cancellation and current authorization.

rbac.note: Community has basic owner and creator boundaries plus MCP permissions; shared projects, fine-grained collaboration and advanced governance require paid editions.

secrets.note: Nodes bind encrypted credential records by reference instead of embedding secrets; external vault integration is separately paid and excluded from this baseline.

isolation.note: Credential ownership and selected input mapping constrain access locally; per-assignment remote tool scopes and tenant isolation need service-specific enforcement.

gates.note: Human tool approvals and conditional paths provide gates; independent reviewer identity and non-bypassable factory-wide acceptance policies require additional enforcement.

stale_decisions.note: Wait callbacks identify executions and tool approvals bind proposed parameters; the baseline does not bind approvals to artifact revisions or automatically reject obsolete evidence.

policy_validation.note: Schema validation and node restrictions provide limited checks; domain policy is custom, while built-in workflow reviews are Enterprise Preview.

learning.note: MCP authoring, test runs and publication support deliberate changes; converting run feedback into tested, governed factory improvements requires a separate authoring capability.

visual_graph.note: The executable node canvas shows manual progress and data; saved production executions expose the executed graph and node results.

history.note: Saved executions show outcomes and errors; complete operator audit streaming and advanced governance are excluded from the free Community baseline.

events.note: APIs and MCP expose execution status for polling; comprehensive lifecycle log streaming is paid, and custom progress requires authored output.

pinned_debug.note: Pinned node outputs and Execute Step support interactive downstream tests; production ignores pins, and past-run Debug in editor requires free registration.

testing.note: MCP test_workflow substitutes supplied outputs and executes logic nodes; credential-free I/O still runs, and comprehensive failure simulation needs additional setup.

fork.note: Past execution data can be loaded into the editor and retried with original or current definitions; this is not arbitrary checkpoint branching.

work_management.note: Workflow owners, tags and execution lists do not constitute a native accountable-goal and escalation layer above individual factory runs.

conversation.note: Chat nodes and human-review channels support conversations and resumed waits; general live-run steering requires an explicit command and authorization design.

incident_cases.note: Error workflows receive failure and retry context; they do not provide a shared incident lifecycle or concurrency-safe symptom-to-case coalescing.

recovery_playbooks.note: Reusable error workflows support recovery actions; approved repair scope, separate edit/publish authority and verified completion require application policy and appropriate permissions.

trace_regressions.note: Saved execution debugging and evaluation datasets reuse production examples; Registered Community enables debugging, while sanitization and immutable trace/revision linkage require integration.

protected_evaluator.note: External Code-node runners support container isolation and read-only filesystems; protecting evaluator definitions and data from candidate-authoring permissions needs additional separation.

candidate_comparison.note: Metric evaluations compare dataset runs; Registered Community covers one workflow. Immutable evaluator/fixture binding and governed keep/reject evidence require additional integration.

scoped_learning_memory.note: Execution records and memory/storage nodes retain data; contract-scoped procedural guidance, rejected-edit reasoning and obsolete-lesson invalidation are not native workflow semantics.

staged_rollout.note: Published versions and paid source-control environments support controlled releases; bounded traffic cohorts and coordinated rollback of their routing require external integration.

research_isolation.note: External task runners isolate code, but queue workers share execution infrastructure; reserved production capacity and separate experiment credentials require independently configured deployments.

proactive_research.note: AI evaluation and workflow loops do not supply a hypothesis-driven campaign controller with allowed mutations, trial decisions and independent campaign stop rules.

version_binding.note: Checkpoint state does not pin executable graph code or dependencies; preserving behavior through deployments requires an application-owned version registry.

dependency_bundle.note: Official Docker guidance packages SDK code and dependencies; factory-specific dependency manifests and environment-binding preflight remain deployment responsibilities.

branch.note: Python edge predicates and TypeScript edge handlers support deterministic conditional routing; custom nodes can expose structured decision results.

parallel_join.note: TypeScript waits for all incoming sources; Python requires explicit all-required predicates because its default join is OR. Failure behavior differs.

dynamic_map.note: SDK code can construct runtime-sized node sets and aggregate dependent results; TypeScript maxConcurrency bounds execution of the constructed graph.

bounded_loop.note: Both SDKs support cyclic edges with execution-count bounds; explicit predicates terminate review loops, while limits produce documented SDK-specific failure outcomes.

advanced_join.note: Conditional edges and node cancellation hooks enable selective routing; quorum accounting, acceptable-result selection and cancellation of surplus remote work need coordination.

nested.note: Graph and Swarm can be nested as nodes in both SDKs; immutable public-contract versions and dependency bindings are not managed.

recursive.note: Custom nodes can reinvoke orchestrators, but graph execution limits are local; recursive depth and shared campaign budgets require explicit application enforcement.

typed_io.note: Pydantic/Zod validate agent outputs and tools can validate inputs; complete factory and remote-assignment schemas require wrappers. TypeScript plain JSON schemas do not validate.

mapping.note: Workflow SDK code and custom graph nodes can select fields or artifact references; default graph propagation includes original input and dependency outputs.

lineage.note: Node identities and telemetry connect dependency executions and outputs; item ancestry, repair revisions and artifact provenance require domain records.

a2a_client.note: Official Python and TypeScript A2AAgent clients resolve Agent Cards, send protocol messages and expose responses through the SDK interface.

a2a_expose.note: Official A2A servers expose agents and cards; exposing a whole Graph factory requires an agent wrapper and explicit factory-contract mapping.

remote_reconcile.note: A2A integration exposes task communication and configurable server task stores; graph checkpoints alone do not reconnect persisted remote assignments after restart.

attempts.note: Graph node IDs, execution counts and tracing identify executions; stable logical remote assignments and durable separate retry-attempt histories need application correlation.

external_dedupe.note: Python offers in-process invocation idempotency tokens; distributed external-effect deduplication and ambiguous-response reconciliation are outside this mechanism. TypeScript lacks those tokens.

artifacts.note: Storage and ContextOffloader support persistent referenced content in local files or S3; configure durable storage and disable eviction for retained artifacts.

artifact_acceptance.note: Structured outputs and stored content do not implement revision-bound acceptance or downstream invalidation after repair; that ledger must be supplied.

durable.note: Configured session managers checkpoint graph progress after nodes and restore it after restart; unfinished work may reexecute, requiring side-effect-safe nodes.

preserve_success.note: Graph restore retains completed nodes and schedules unfinished work; incomplete TypeScript nested orchestrators restart internally unless separately persisted. Terminal reruns can start fresh.

retries.note: Provider retries expose bounded backoff; hooks implement classified tool retries. Durable, declarative retry policies for arbitrary graph nodes are not provided.

timeouts.note: Both graph SDKs expose execution and node deadlines. TypeScript deadlines are cooperative and do not automatically propagate into nested orchestrators.

waits.note: Graph interrupts can persist awaiting correlated input across restart; durable timed wakeups and timer dispatch require an external scheduler.

commands.note: Interrupt responses carry unique IDs and route to paused nodes; arbitrary live commands, authorization and domain-level input validation need a service interface.

cancel.note: Hooks cancel pending nodes and agent signals stop cooperative work; nested and remote cancellation policies with reconciled final outcomes need additional coordination.

unknown.note: The documented A2A wrapper and graph state do not provide an authoritative uncertain-dispatch ledger that reconciles effects before resubmission.

compensation.note: Ordinary workflow SDK code can catch failures and invoke compensating tools; application-defined error handlers specify the recovery sequence for reversible effects.

triggers.note: Direct SDK calls and A2A servers provide invocation entry points; event subscriptions and scheduled starts belong to deployment infrastructure.

catchup.note: The in-process SDK has no native durable schedule service or missed-trigger catch-up policy; scheduling infrastructure must supply these semantics.

overlap.note: Single-agent concurrency guards reject overlapping invocations; workflow-wide queue, skip and coalesce policies across processes require an admission layer.

capacity.note: TypeScript graphs bound local node concurrency and Python workflow tools bound thread pools; distributed admission queues and reserved cross-factory capacity remain external.

priority.note: The Python workflow tool sorts ready tasks by numeric priority; no distributed fairness policy or equivalent Graph priority scheduler is documented.

ownership.note: Session managers explicitly take no distributed lock; competing processes can overwrite state, so authoritative attempt fencing requires an external ownership mechanism.

budget.note: Per-invocation token caps and telemetry provide useful accounting; caps can overshoot within a turn and do not enforce shared monetary admission budgets.

eligibility.note: No native reconciler tracks external assignment ownership or permission changes against live factories; tool policies alone do not supply that lifecycle.

rbac.note: Cedar authorizes identity-aware tool calls in both SDKs; author, publisher and workflow-operator permissions require a separate control-plane authorization model.

secrets.note: Model clients support environment-supplied credentials and configured authenticated clients, allowing SDK applications to bind secrets outside graph code and task documents.

isolation.note: Per-context A2A factories, invocation metadata and Cedar tool policies provide isolation primitives; remote services must enforce their own data and credential boundaries.

gates.note: Interrupts and conditional edges can gate downstream publication; reviewer independence and non-bypassable publication authority require explicit service and policy design.

stale_decisions.note: Interrupt IDs correlate responses but do not reject approvals against changed artifact revisions or superseded business state; revision authority requires application logic.

policy_validation.note: Graph construction and Cedar schema checks validate structure and tool policy; approved identities, global bounds and mandatory factory acceptance paths need domain checks.

learning.note: Python Evals diagnoses existing traces and evaluates changes; continuously publishing governed factory revisions requires an engineering controller and separate release authority.

visual_graph.note: SDK topology, node status and progress events are available programmatically; a built-in visual factory graph and live execution console are not supplied.

history.note: OpenTelemetry captures execution inputs, outputs, errors and metrics; durable queryable run history and operator audit records require configured observability and application storage.

events.note: Both SDKs expose multi-agent lifecycle hooks and streaming node events, allowing applications to consume progress, completions, interrupts and failures programmatically.

pinned_debug.note: Evaluation result caching exists, but the SDK has no visual node-pinning interface or interactive downstream graph execution using saved node outputs.

testing.note: Python Evals supports controlled tool failures and simulations; deterministic graph-routing assertions using supplied node results still require SDK test fixtures.

fork.note: Agent snapshots support historical restore and conversation branching; graph history forks and external-effect semantics are not automatically supplied by snapshot restoration.

work_management.note: Agent goals and workflow tasks do not constitute an accountable work-management layer with persistent owners, decision authority and escalation cases.

conversation.note: A2A input-required tasks and graph interrupts support conversational interaction; translating conversation into authorized run operations remains application-owned.

incident_cases.note: Python Evals deduplicates diagnostic recommendations within results, but does not atomically coalesce cross-run incidents into durably owned operational cases.

recovery_playbooks.note: Reusable SDK workflows lack a native versioned recovery-playbook registry with scoped repair authority, verified postconditions and independent publication permissions.

trace_regressions.note: Python Evals ingests production traces and serializes cases and reports; sanitization, expected outcomes and factory/contract revision links require fixture governance.

protected_evaluator.note: Docker/SSH sandboxes and tool allowlists can constrain candidate execution; protected evaluator mounts, immutable data and mutation permissions require deployment configuration.

candidate_comparison.note: Python Evals reuses serialized cases and evaluators across implementations; pinned comparison policy, cost/latency tradeoffs, uncertainty and keep/reject decisions require application logic.

scoped_learning_memory.note: Persistent memory and serialized evaluation reports retain useful evidence; rejected-change records and revision-scoped lesson applicability need an explicit domain schema.

staged_rollout.note: No native factory version router, bounded new-run cohort release or audited rollback controller exists in the SDK; deployment infrastructure must provide them.

research_isolation.note: Sandbox backends and separate credential configurations support isolated evaluation; worker-pool reservation and production capacity guarantees require external infrastructure.

proactive_research.note: Python Evals provides experiments and stored reports; opt-in hypothesis campaigns, editable-surface limits, shared budgets and durable keep/reject control require orchestration.

selectionAssessment.label: Potential infrastructure blocker
selectionAssessment.license: Apache 2.0 SDK; hosted AgentCore is optional
selectionAssessment.known: The SDK has a permissive license. Graph coordination and session persistence do not supply the entire durable factory platform. Session management does not provide distributed locking against competing writers.
selectionAssessment.condition: A blocker as the outer factory runtime if supplying a durable execution host, attempt ownership and a governed publication service exceeds the accepted custom-infrastructure budget.
selectionAssessment.path: Use Strands inside independently callable agent services. It is removed from the primary outer-runtime shortlist under the minimal-infrastructure preference, while remaining scored and selectable. Reconsider as the outer runtime only after explicitly accepting and proving the additional hosting, ownership and publication platform.

langgraph.name: LangGraph
langgraph.baseline: Open-source Python LangGraph with official persistent checkpointers/stores and synchronous checkpoint durability configured for production. Current official docs assessed 2026-09-21, including documented 1.2 APIs; no release pinned or runtime conformance tested. LangSmith Agent Server, Studio, evaluation and Engine features are outside this OSS baseline and receive at most partial support. Ordinary SDK graph code counts for general execution; bespoke factory subsystems do not.

native_definition.note: StateGraph defines nodes and routing in application code; langgraph.json selects Python/JavaScript graph entrypoints rather than supplying an executable factory document.

publish_no_deploy.note: New compositions ordinarily require new graph code. Assistant configuration can parameterize existing code, but a general document interpreter would be an additional application subsystem.

schema_discovery.note: Graph state and configuration schemas describe coded interfaces; no native catalog exposes arbitrary reusable task primitives as an authoring vocabulary.

validate_only.note: Compilation checks graph structure before invocation, and tests run locally; validating a native published factory document is outside this code-based model.

agent_authoring.note: The official CLI builds and runs graph applications; publication still deploys application code. LangSmith deployment tooling does not turn graph code into native factory documents.

version_binding.note: Resumed threads use the latest graph. Official guidance offers state-stamped behavioral versions and preserved code paths; automatic immutable code binding is absent.

dependency_bundle.note: CLI packaging includes graph entrypoints and dependencies in an application image; factory capability bindings and environment compatibility preflight remain additional checks.

branch.note: Edges, conditional routers and Command updates directly express sequences and branches on structured state.

parallel_join.note: Parallel supersteps and list-form dependency edges implement all-required joins; failed branches have explicit error and retry behavior.

dynamic_map.note: Send creates runtime-sized fan-out, reducers aggregate results, and max_concurrency bounds concurrent graph tasks.

bounded_loop.note: Conditional cycles and the enforced superstep recursion limit bound review loops; coded conditions select stop or escalation paths.

advanced_join.note: Reducers and conditional code can count acceptable results, but ordinary parallel supersteps wait for their tasks; quorum racing and surplus-work cancellation need additional coordination.

nested.note: Compiled subgraphs provide reusable inputs, outputs and nested persistence; preserving an independently versioned subfactory requires application packaging and version routing.

recursive.note: Graphs can invoke graphs, but recursion_limit counts execution supersteps, not a global cross-invocation call-depth or spend budget; recursive factory admission needs explicit guards.

typed_io.note: Pydantic validates initial inputs; current documentation explicitly excludes subsequent-node and output validation. TypedDict/output schemas do not establish complete runtime contract validation.

mapping.note: Node functions select state fields and explicitly transform inputs and outputs when calling subgraphs with different schemas.

lineage.note: Checkpoint/task identities and state history expose execution ancestry; item-to-artifact provenance and repair revision links must be modeled in application state.

a2a_client.note: Official A2A examples construct JSON-RPC HTTP calls. The OSS graph runtime has no native remote A2A lifecycle client; RemoteGraph uses the separate Agent Server API.

a2a_expose.note: LangSmith Agent Server exposes an Agent Card and A2A endpoint for assistants; that server capability sits outside the open-source runtime baseline.

remote_reconcile.note: Checkpoints can retain remote IDs and RemoteGraph can inspect remote state; reconnecting arbitrary A2A tasks after ambiguous dispatch requires a service-specific adapter.

attempts.note: Execution info exposes thread, run, checkpoint, task and attempt identifiers. Complete retained attempt history and its remote assignment mapping need tracing or application records.

external_dedupe.note: Checkpointed results do not atomically commit external effects. Concurrent deduplication and ambiguous-response reconciliation require provider idempotency or an application-owned protocol.

artifacts.note: Persistent stores retain retrievable namespaced records, and graph state can carry artifact references. Binary/object storage and artifact retention contracts need an external storage binding.

artifact_acceptance.note: Checkpoint revisions identify graph state; they do not supply artifact acceptance records or automatically invalidate approval after a repaired artifact changes.

durable.note: A persistent checkpointer with sync durability saves progress before continuing; invocation with the same thread can recover after failure. In-memory and exit-only modes do not provide this guarantee.

preserve_success.note: Pending checkpoint writes retain successful sibling-node outputs when another node in the same superstep fails, so recorded successful work is skipped on recovery.

retries.note: Per-node RetryPolicy supports exception predicates, maximum attempts, exponential backoff, interval ceilings and jitter.

timeouts.note: Documented 1.2 node policies enforce async-attempt run/idle timeouts and exhaustion handlers. Synchronous nodes and end-to-end durable factory deadlines need additional handling.

waits.note: Checkpointed interrupts survive restart and await external decisions. Persistent time-based wakeups require a scheduler or Agent Server integration beyond the core runtime.

commands.note: Thread-scoped Command resumptions and interrupt IDs correlate decisions; documented validation loops reject invalid input before the graph proceeds.

cancel.note: Async execution can be interrupted, and Agent Server supplies run cancellation. Parent/child abandonment policies and reconciliation of remote effects need explicit application logic.

unknown.note: Durable state and interrupts can preserve an unknown outcome while a reconciliation node runs; the remote-action uncertainty model and safe resubmission conditions are application-defined.

compensation.note: Documented node error handlers run after retry exhaustion and can route to application-defined compensating steps with Command.

triggers.note: Core invoke APIs start graphs; HTTP run APIs and recurring cron jobs come from Agent Server, while external event intake requires an integration.

catchup.note: The OSS runtime supplies no scheduler or missed-start policy. Reviewed Agent Server cron documentation does not establish configurable downtime catch-up semantics.

overlap.note: Agent Server supports enqueue, reject, interrupt and rollback strategies for overlapping thread runs; documentation explicitly excludes these controls from OSS LangGraph.

capacity.note: max_concurrency bounds tasks in one graph invocation. Shared run queues, deployment worker capacity and admission across factories require Agent Server or external infrastructure.

priority.note: The reviewed core and deployment controls bound concurrency but do not provide a documented factory task-priority and fair-dispatch contract.

ownership.note: Timed-out attempts discard buffered writes. Cross-process thread claims and stale-worker fencing are not an OSS checkpointer guarantee; hosted overlap controls address only part of the requirement.

budget.note: LangSmith attributes LLM and custom component cost to traces. Atomic budget admission, in-flight reservations and stopping remote factory spend remain application responsibilities.

eligibility.note: Invocation and interrupts expose control points, but no built-in reconciler tracks changing external work ownership and revokes active factory eligibility.

rbac.note: Agent Server offers per-resource authorization handlers outside the OSS runtime. Distinct authoring, publication and recovery roles still require an explicit policy.

secrets.note: Applications and CLI deployment configuration can bind environment credentials; secret storage, rotation and narrowly scoped service credential issuance remain hosting concerns.

isolation.note: Thread and per-invocation subgraph namespaces isolate context. Enforcing remote tool permissions and data access requires authorization and service boundaries beyond state schemas.

gates.note: Interrupts and conditional transitions enforce coded review paths; reviewer independence and a publication gate that authors cannot bypass need external policy enforcement.

stale_decisions.note: Interrupt IDs and validation loops correlate resumed input. Comparing the approved artifact revision with authoritative current state is an application rule, not a built-in approval guarantee.

policy_validation.note: Graph compilation validates structure, not capability allowlists, publication authority, mandatory quality paths or global factory budgets.

learning.note: LangSmith Engine detects trace issues and proposes code fixes with regression examples. It is a separate platform service; protected evaluation and governed factory publication remain additional policy.

visual_graph.note: The SDK renders graph structure; LangSmith Studio adds interactive graph execution and state views outside the OSS runtime baseline.

history.note: Persistent state history records checkpoints and execution errors. Comprehensive operator audit and retained tracing require additional instrumentation or LangSmith.

events.note: Streaming exposes state updates, values, task/debug information, custom progress and nested-subgraph events through programmatic APIs.

pinned_debug.note: State updates and checkpoint forks permit downstream experiments; Studio adds interactive state editing, but that visual surface is outside the OSS baseline.

testing.note: Documented tests compile graphs with isolated checkpointers, exercise individual nodes and resume selected sections; ordinary test substitutes can supply node results and failures.

fork.note: Checkpoint IDs support replay and update_state creates a new branch. Nodes after the fork execute again, including external side effects unless separately guarded.

work_management.note: Thread and run management do not provide factory goals, accountable supervisors, external work ownership or escalation policy as a native domain model.

conversation.note: Message state and interrupt resumptions support conversational steering; Studio offers chat mode, while authorized command interpretation and factory supervision semantics are application-defined.

incident_cases.note: Separate LangSmith Engine groups recurring trace issues and retains evidence. Atomic case ownership, coalesced recovery attempts and maintenance resolution authority need additional machinery.

recovery_playbooks.note: Reusable subgraphs and recovery routing can execute approved repair steps; version pinning, scoped repair authority and mandatory verification need application policy.

trace_regressions.note: LangSmith can turn trace evidence into versioned dataset examples. Sanitization, factory/contract revision binding and authoritative expected outcomes remain publication checks.

protected_evaluator.note: Separate evaluation datasets and resource authorization provide building blocks in LangSmith; confining candidate code and preventing evaluator/test modification require deployment isolation.

candidate_comparison.note: LangSmith compares experiments on shared datasets with feedback and performance metrics. Pinned evaluator integrity, uncertainty and an authoritative keep/reject decision need additional controls.

scoped_learning_memory.note: Namespaced stores retain arbitrary records, but rejected-change ledgers, evidence-backed lesson applicability and contract/policy revision invalidation are not native factory semantics.

staged_rollout.note: Assistant configurations support version rollback and application state can route behavioral versions. Bounded cohort admission and immutable active code bindings require separate deployment policy.

research_isolation.note: Separate deployments and credentials can separate production and evaluation. Reserved capacity and restrictions on experimental effects are infrastructure and authorization configuration beyond the SDK.

proactive_research.note: Graphs and evaluation tools can be assembled into experiments, but no native opt-in campaign component owns objectives, editable resources, combined limits and the keep/reject ledger.

selectionAssessment.label: Excluded by decision
selectionAssessment.license: MIT core; separately licensed deployment platform
selectionAssessment.known: The MIT core can run in an independently hosted production application. The packaged production Agent Server requires a license; its dev server is a development/testing path. A configurable concurrency default is not a verified artificial performance cap.
selectionAssessment.condition: Already excluded by the owner because the platform's commercial self-hosting constraints are unacceptable.
selectionAssessment.path: Retain its feature evidence and scores for comparison. A custom host around the MIT library is technically possible, but does not reverse this decision or put LangGraph back on the shortlist.

features.name: Native executable factory document
features.requirement: Publish a graph as JSON/YAML rather than new workflow application code.
features.importanceRationale: A native executable document is central to agent-authored factories without a custom interpreter.

conductor.note: Canonical JSON is stored, versioned and executed by the engine; SDK authoring produces the same native definition document.

kestra.note: Native YAML declares tasks, inputs, outputs and orchestration; the server stores and runs flow definitions without generating orchestration application code.

temporal.note: Workflow definitions are SDK application code; the server does not execute arbitrary JSON or YAML graphs as native factory definitions.

n8n.note: Native workflow JSON describes nodes, connections and settings; imported definitions execute using installed node implementations without separate orchestration application code.

langgraph.note: StateGraph defines nodes and routing in application code; langgraph.json selects Python/JavaScript graph entrypoints rather than supplying an executable factory document.

strands.note: Graph is code-defined; the Python community workflow tool accepts persisted JSON task lists, with a narrower dependency-based execution model.

windmill.note: OpenFlow is a native executable JSON/YAML document containing modules, data mappings and control flow; existing scripts and flows can be referenced.

argo.note: Workflow and WorkflowTemplate Kubernetes resources contain executable YAML/JSON DAGs or steps; the controller interprets their declared template composition.

features.name: Publish compositions without a worker deployment
features.requirement: Reuse existing task implementations for a newly published factory.
features.importanceRationale: Routine new compositions must reuse existing services without deploying orchestration code.

conductor.note: New definitions reuse existing workers and built-in tasks; registering another composition does not require redeploying those implementations.

kestra.note: New YAML compositions can be deployed through CLI/API using installed plugins; no worker deployment is required for rearranging existing primitives.

temporal.note: New orchestration logic must reach compatible Workers; a reusable document interpreter would be additional application infrastructure beyond the baseline.

n8n.note: Saving and publishing a workflow activates a composition of existing nodes; only new node implementations require installation or deployment.

langgraph.note: New compositions ordinarily require new graph code. Assistant configuration can parameterize existing code, but a general document interpreter would be an additional application subsystem.

strands.note: Python workflow task lists reuse loaded tools without redeployment; arbitrary Graph compositions still require application construction and a publication layer.

windmill.note: Deploying an OpenFlow composition registers its definition for existing workers; rearranging existing scripts or service adapters needs no separate worker deployment.

argo.note: Register a WorkflowTemplate or submit a new Workflow using existing container, HTTP and plugin templates; new compositions require no controller deployment.

features.name: External-agent authoring tools
features.requirement: Supported MCP/CLI/API path to create, validate and publish definitions.
features.importanceRationale: External agents need a supported route to author, validate and publish factories.

conductor.note: Official CLI and REST operations support authoring, validation, registration and execution; external agents can operate these documented interfaces.

kestra.note: External-agent skills combine live schemas with CLI validation, deployment and execution; documentation MCP itself supplies context rather than running flows.

temporal.note: Official agent skills and CLI support writing and operating workflow code; native document creation and publication still require a custom authoring layer.

n8n.note: Instance MCP supports discovery, validation, creation, editing, testing and publication for authorized external clients on self-hosted installations.

langgraph.note: The official CLI builds and runs graph applications; publication still deploys application code. LangSmith deployment tooling does not turn graph code into native factory documents.

strands.note: The Python workflow tool supports create/start/status using task documents; independent validation, immutable publication and arbitrary Graph authoring need additional tooling.

windmill.note: Official CLI development, YAML validation and MCP create/update operations support external agents authoring and publishing flows; MCP alone is not the validator.

argo.note: Supported CLI, Kubernetes and REST APIs let external agents validate, create and submit workflow definitions; no native MCP authoring server is assumed.

features.name: Run definition and version isolation
features.requirement: Record a run’s definition/code binding and preserve active-run behavior during updates.
features.importanceRationale: Updates and repairs must preserve the contract governing active executions.

conductor.note: Active executions retain their starting definition snapshot through updates; recorded snapshots also govern ordinary retries and restarts.

kestra.note: Every flow change creates a revision and drafts stay unpublished; child references can pin revisions instead of selecting the latest.

temporal.note: Pinned Worker Deployment Versions preserve code binding for active Workflows; independent Activities require their own compatible deployment and version policy.

n8n.note: Draft and published graph versions are distinct, and saved executions retain original workflow data; settings and referenced dependencies are not fully frozen.

langgraph.note: Resumed threads use the latest graph. Official guidance offers state-stamped behavioral versions and preserved code paths; automatic immutable code binding is absent.

strands.note: Checkpoint state does not pin executable graph code or dependencies; preserving behavior through deployments requires an application-owned version registry.

windmill.note: Jobs retain flow snapshots and script hashes; Workflow SDK executions pin their original script version. Referenced child paths require explicit version selection.

argo.note: Runs retain specifications and resolved templates; unresolved references resolve by name. Immutable version-named dependencies need publication enforcement; Secure mode errors on template changes.

features.name: Machine-readable primitive schemas
features.requirement: Discover available task types, inputs and options for authoring.
features.importanceRationale: Machine-readable primitives improve reliable authoring and reduce integration effort.

conductor.note: Published JSON Schemas describe workflow, task and runtime objects; metadata APIs expose registered task and workflow definitions.

kestra.note: The documentation MCP exposes plugin schemas, options and versions; live instance schemas help authors match the actual available task catalog.

temporal.note: SDK types describe registered interfaces, but there is no native discoverable catalog of arbitrary deployed Activity input and output schemas.

n8n.note: Built-in MCP node search and type retrieval expose exact parameter structures; node configuration validation checks generated schemas before composition.

langgraph.note: Graph state and configuration schemas describe coded interfaces; no native catalog exposes arbitrary reusable task primitives as an authoring vocabulary.

strands.note: Tool specifications expose machine-readable inputs; graph constructors expose SDK types, without a complete discoverable catalog of publishable factory primitives.

windmill.note: The canonical OpenAPI OpenFlow schema describes module options; script, resource and flow inputs expose machine-readable JSON schemas for authoring.

argo.note: Published JSON Schema and Kubernetes resource schemas describe workflow primitives and options; plugin-specific configuration contracts still belong to their implementations.

features.name: Validate without publishing
features.requirement: Receive actionable definition validation errors without registering a live flow.
features.importanceRationale: Prepublication feedback makes agent iteration faster; all published candidates still require validation.

conductor.note: The workflow validation endpoint checks a candidate definition without saving it and returns structured invalid-definition error details.

kestra.note: The supported CLI validates candidate flow files before deployment and returns errors without replacing a published flow definition.

temporal.note: SDK compilation, sandbox checks, tests and replay validate code before deployment; there is no declarative factory validation endpoint.

n8n.note: MCP validate_workflow returns errors and warnings before creation; validate_node_config separately checks individual parameter schemas without publishing a workflow.

langgraph.note: Compilation checks graph structure before invocation, and tests run locally; validating a native published factory document is outside this code-based model.

strands.note: Python GraphBuilder validates on build before execution; neither SDK supplies a separate factory-document validation/publication service with comprehensive contract checks.

windmill.note: The supported VS Code YAML linter validates flow definitions before deployment; schema-based feedback is available without registering a production flow.

argo.note: Argo lint validates workflows and referenced templates, including strict checks and offline bundles; submission also supports server dry-run validation.

features.name: Portable dependency bundle
features.requirement: Package definitions and referenced dependencies with environment binding checks.
features.importanceRationale: Portable packaging can follow a working deployment with explicit dependency bindings.

conductor.note: Definitions and task metadata are exportable, but assembling worker artifacts, integrations and environment compatibility remains deployment integration work.

kestra.note: YAML and namespace files are portable components; dependency/environment checks require deployment tooling, with richer packaging and promotion features in Enterprise.

temporal.note: Worker application packaging is external deployment work; no native factory package bundles definitions, capability dependencies and environment preflight checks.
