n8n.note: Preview packages include workflows and dependencies with preflight checks; secrets remain environment bindings, and some packaged resources require paid licenses.

langgraph.note: CLI packaging includes graph entrypoints and dependencies in an application image; factory capability bindings and environment compatibility preflight remain additional checks.

strands.note: Official Docker guidance packages SDK code and dependencies; factory-specific dependency manifests and environment-binding preflight remain deployment responsibilities.

windmill.note: CLI projects carry flow documents, inline scripts and lockfiles; environment-specific credentials and dependency bindings need deployment configuration rather than universal bundle validation.

argo.note: Offline lint can resolve templates supplied together; portable container images, secrets, artifact stores and environment compatibility still require deployment-level packaging and checks.

features.name: Bounded review and repair loops
features.requirement: Repeat work under an explicit limit and stop/escalation condition.
features.importanceRationale: Review, repair and maintenance must always have enforceable stopping conditions.

conductor.note: DO_WHILE conditions can bound iterations and route exhaustion; configured workflow and task timeouts provide additional explicit execution limits.

kestra.note: LoopUntil accepts maximum iterations and duration; configure failOnMaxReached or explicit routing because reaching limits otherwise defaults to successful completion.

temporal.note: Ordinary deterministic loops enforce explicit iteration limits and escalation outcomes; Continue-As-New can bound history for lengthy repeated processes.

n8n.note: Loop Over Items and conditional back-edges express repeated processing; explicit counters and conditions bound review loops and choose escalation outcomes.

langgraph.note: Conditional cycles and the enforced superstep recursion limit bound review loops; coded conditions select stop or escalation paths.

strands.note: Both SDKs support cyclic edges with execution-count bounds; explicit predicates terminate review loops, while limits produce documented SDK-specific failure outcomes.

windmill.note: While loops expose iteration state and early-stop predicates; definitions can enforce an iteration ceiling, branch on acceptance and route exhausted work.

argo.note: Finite loops and recursive templates with explicit counter conditions express bounded repair; workflow/template deadlines provide additional enforced termination limits.

features.name: Versioned nested factories
features.requirement: Invoke a reusable subworkflow with public inputs, outputs and a version binding.
features.importanceRationale: Reusable factory composition is a defining requirement of the service catalog.

conductor.note: SUB_WORKFLOW specifies child name, version and mapped inputs; its outputs and execution identity are available to the parent.

kestra.note: Subflow binds namespace, flow ID and optional revision, maps inputs/outputs, and configures waiting and propagation of child failure.

temporal.note: Child Workflows provide inputs, results and parent relationships; Worker Versioning supplies code binding, subject to independently versioned child deployment configuration.

n8n.note: Subworkflows expose typed input fields and parent-child execution links, but the invocation node does not provide an explicit immutable version selector.

langgraph.note: Compiled subgraphs provide reusable inputs, outputs and nested persistence; preserving an independently versioned subfactory requires application packaging and version routing.

strands.note: Graph and Swarm can be nested as nodes in both SDKs; immutable public-contract versions and dependency bindings are not managed.

windmill.note: The native runFlowByVersion API accepts arguments and parent-job correlation for pinned child calls; OpenFlow PathFlow nodes themselves reference current paths.

argo.note: Reusable templates expose parameters and artifacts, but templateRef names carry no immutable version field; versioned resource names and publication restrictions must establish bindings.

features.name: Validated input and result schemas
features.requirement: Runtime validation of both assignment inputs and step/factory result shape.
features.importanceRationale: Validated assignments and results make independently implemented services composable.

conductor.note: Runtime schemas exist, but externalized task outputs and asynchronous system-task outputs bypass checks; missing registry documents can silently disable enforcement.

kestra.note: Inputs support typed and JSON-schema validation; arbitrary remote result and intermediate output contracts need explicit validation steps beyond declared output fields.

temporal.note: Full with Python plus the official Pydantic converter and concrete declared types. Configure validation at every relevant Workflow and Activity input/result boundary.

n8n.note: Subworkflow inputs can declare names and types; universal runtime validation of every step and factory output schema is not automatic.

langgraph.note: Pydantic validates initial inputs; current documentation explicitly excludes subsequent-node and output validation. TypedDict/output schemas do not establish complete runtime contract validation.

strands.note: Pydantic/Zod validate agent outputs and tools can validate inputs; complete factory and remote-assignment schemas require wrappers. TypeScript plain JSON schemas do not validate.

windmill.note: Input JSON schemas and parameter inference provide structured contracts; general step and flow outputs do not receive universal runtime result-schema enforcement.

argo.note: Required parameters and enum values receive validation, but parameter/result values are not generally checked against capability JSON Schemas; reusable validators remain necessary.

features.name: Item and artifact lineage
features.requirement: Trace outputs through fan-out, merges and repair to their originating inputs.
features.importanceRationale: Review and repair need reliable links from input and attempt to the exact output revision.

conductor.note: Execution records preserve task references, iterations and outputs; semantic item identities and artifact transformation lineage require explicit metadata.

kestra.note: Task-run identities and stored output references preserve execution provenance; semantic item mapping and artifact-revision lineage need additional domain metadata.

temporal.note: History relates Activity inputs, outputs and execution events; semantic artifact ancestry through aggregation and repair requires application identifiers.

n8n.note: Native item links trace outputs to inputs through splits and merges. Artifact-revision ancestry and repair lineage need explicit application metadata.

langgraph.note: Checkpoint/task identities and state history expose execution ancestry; item-to-artifact provenance and repair revision links must be modeled in application state.

strands.note: Node identities and telemetry connect dependency executions and outputs; item ancestry, repair revisions and artifact provenance require domain records.

windmill.note: Jobs retain iteration inputs and results, while Assets tracks supported reads/writes; exact artifact-revision lineage through arbitrary repairs requires additional domain metadata.

argo.note: Persisted node identities, relationships and outputs expose execution provenance; immutable artifact revisions and lineage across repairs require application identifiers and records.

features.name: Sequence and conditional routing
features.requirement: Branch on explicit conditions and structured results.
features.importanceRationale: Basic routing supports every factory; its initial behavior is simple and well specified.

conductor.note: Native task sequences and SWITCH operators route using workflow inputs or structured task outputs through explicit configured branches.

kestra.note: Sequential, If, Switch and DAG primitives route structured outputs through explicit configured conditions and dependencies without an LLM choosing every transition.

temporal.note: Deterministic SDK control flow directly expresses sequences, structured conditions and branches; external nondeterministic operations execute as Activities.

n8n.note: If and Switch nodes route structured items through explicit conditions; connected ordinary nodes define sequential transformations and actions.

langgraph.note: Edges, conditional routers and Command updates directly express sequences and branches on structured state.

strands.note: Python edge predicates and TypeScript edge handlers support deterministic conditional routing; custom nodes can expose structured decision results.

windmill.note: Branch-one modules evaluate ordered expressions over structured inputs/results, select the first matching branch and provide an explicit default path.

argo.note: Sequential steps, DAG dependencies, when conditions and expression tags route execution using explicit task outputs and structured JSON expressions.

features.name: Parallel branches and all-required join
features.requirement: Declare dependencies and wait for all required results with explicit failure behavior.
features.importanceRationale: All-required joins support the representative factory; advanced coordination can grow from this basic primitive.

conductor.note: Fork and JOIN operators express parallel task dependencies; optional-task and failure settings specify which failures may be tolerated.

kestra.note: Parallel and DAG tasks express required dependencies and completion; AllowFailure and configured error behavior govern tolerated branch failures.

temporal.note: SDK futures and asynchronous Activities support concurrent branches, all-required joins and explicit exception handling in normal Workflow code.

n8n.note: Merge supports joining branch data, but ordinary branches execute sequentially; truly concurrent sub-executions need additional coordination and explicit failure collection.

langgraph.note: Parallel supersteps and list-form dependency edges implement all-required joins; failed branches have explicit error and retry behavior.

strands.note: TypeScript waits for all incoming sources; Python requires explicit all-required predicates because its default join is OR. Failure behavior differs.

windmill.note: Branch-all executes declared branches concurrently and joins their results; per-branch skip-failure settings make the required completion behavior explicit.

argo.note: DAG dependency edges and parallel steps wait for required predecessors; failFast controls whether independent branches continue after a failure.

features.name: Runtime-sized parallel map
features.requirement: Create per-item tasks at runtime with aggregation and bounded concurrency.
features.importanceRationale: Runtime fan-out adds useful workload flexibility after the core execution contract works.

conductor.note: Dynamic forks create runtime-selected per-item work and JOIN collects results; task-definition concurrency limits cap execution of worker tasks.

kestra.note: Loop expands a runtime collection into per-item work, supports concurrency limits and makes iteration outputs available for downstream aggregation.

temporal.note: Workflow code starts runtime-sized Activity or child sets, applies bounded batches or semaphores, and collects results through SDK concurrency primitives.

n8n.note: Item processing and per-item subworkflows handle runtime-sized inputs; bounded concurrent fan-out with aggregation requires additional coordination beyond ordinary sequential branches.

langgraph.note: Send creates runtime-sized fan-out, reducers aggregate results, and max_concurrency bounds concurrent graph tasks.

strands.note: SDK code can construct runtime-sized node sets and aggregate dependent results; TypeScript maxConcurrency bounds execution of the constructed graph.

windmill.note: For-loop modules evaluate runtime item lists, retain per-iteration results and support an explicit parallelism cap with configurable failure handling.

argo.note: withParam expands runtime JSON arrays into task instances, aggregates outputs, and combines with template parallelism or synchronization to bound concurrency.

features.name: Explicit input/output mapping
features.requirement: Pass selected data or artifact references between steps.
features.importanceRationale: Explicit data mapping is required integration plumbing rather than a major engine discriminator.

conductor.note: Task input parameters and workflow output expressions explicitly select upstream fields, structured values or artifact references for each boundary.

kestra.note: Expressions select task outputs and file URIs, while explicit flow outputs define the public results passed to parent workflows.

temporal.note: Workflow code explicitly selects and transforms Activity results into subsequent arguments, including object-store references instead of entire artifacts.

n8n.note: Expressions and the visual mapper select prior node fields into downstream parameters, including identifiers and artifact references through branches.

langgraph.note: Node functions select state fields and explicitly transform inputs and outputs when calling subgraphs with different schemas.

strands.note: Workflow SDK code and custom graph nodes can select fields or artifact references; default graph propagation includes original input and dependency outputs.

windmill.note: Static and JavaScript input transforms explicitly map flow inputs, earlier results and iteration values into each script or subflow assignment.

argo.note: Named parameters, artifact references and expression mappings pass selected inputs and outputs through tasks, loops and nested templates.

features.name: First acceptable result or quorum
features.requirement: Wait for acceptable results rather than raw completion; handle surplus work.
features.importanceRationale: All-required joins cover the first factories; quorum and first-acceptable patterns can wait.

conductor.note: EXCLUSIVE_JOIN supplies first-completion behavior, but acceptance predicates, quorum accounting and reconciliation of surplus remote work need additional orchestration.

kestra.note: The documented core flow vocabulary supplies Parallel/Dag completion joins, not an acceptance-aware race or quorum operator with surplus-work reconciliation.

temporal.note: SDK-authored acceptance or quorum logic uses asynchronous completion and cancellation primitives. This is normal Workflow code, not a turnkey acceptance-aware operator.

n8n.note: Merge is a data-combination primitive; there is no native quorum or first-acceptable completion join that cancels surplus remote work.

langgraph.note: Reducers and conditional code can count acceptable results, but ordinary parallel supersteps wait for their tasks; quorum racing and surplus-work cancellation need additional coordination.

strands.note: Conditional edges and node cancellation hooks enable selective routing; quorum accounting, acceptable-result selection and cancellation of surplus remote work need coordination.

windmill.note: Branch-all joins completion; approval event counts do not implement first-acceptable task results, semantic quorum aggregation or coordinated cancellation of surplus work.

argo.note: Dependency expressions support task-result predicates and AnySucceeded/AllFailed aggregates; acceptance-aware quorum selection and cancellation of surplus remote work require orchestration logic.

features.name: Bounded recursive factory calls
features.requirement: Support direct or indirect self-invocation with enforced depth/budget bounds.
features.importanceRationale: Versioned nesting meets initial composition needs without self-recursive calls.

conductor.note: Dynamic child-workflow invocation supplies composition primitives; a depth counter and shared recursion budget must be enforced in the definition.

kestra.note: The subflow contract explicitly prohibits direct and indirect recursive calls; bounded iteration must use loop primitives instead of cyclic subflow invocation.

temporal.note: Child Workflows may invoke the same type, but depth and shared-budget enforcement are explicitly authored application guards rather than a native recursive-call contract.

n8n.note: Subworkflow calls and conditional guards permit bounded composition, but recursion depth and shared budget enforcement require explicit workflow state and checks.

langgraph.note: Graphs can invoke graphs, but recursion_limit counts execution supersteps, not a global cross-invocation call-depth or spend budget; recursive factory admission needs explicit guards.

strands.note: Custom nodes can reinvoke orchestrators, but graph execution limits are local; recursive depth and shared campaign budgets require explicit application enforcement.

windmill.note: Subflow calls and SDK orchestration permit recursive composition, but shared recursion-depth and budget enforcement must be explicitly authored around those calls.

argo.note: Templates can invoke themselves recursively. Depth counters, shared budget propagation and authorization bounds must be explicitly implemented in the approved composition.

features.name: Native remote A2A task client
features.requirement: Handle discovery/task messages using an explicit supported A2A integration.
features.importanceRationale: Native remote-agent integration directly reduces custom lifecycle infrastructure.

conductor.note: Native AGENT, GET_AGENT_CARD and CANCEL_AGENT tasks handle supported A2A calls; protocol compatibility still requires checking the selected release.

kestra.note: The free AI plugin provides a native A2A prompt proxy; its documented contract exposes text output rather than comprehensive task lifecycle controls.

temporal.note: Official SDK baseline has no built-in A2A task client; an Activity wrapping an A2A library is application integration.

n8n.note: The built-in integration baseline does not document a native A2A task client; HTTP requests alone do not implement A2A lifecycle semantics.

langgraph.note: Official A2A examples construct JSON-RPC HTTP calls. The OSS graph runtime has no native remote A2A lifecycle client; RemoteGraph uses the separate Agent Server API.

strands.note: Official Python and TypeScript A2AAgent clients resolve Agent Cards, send protocol messages and expose responses through the SDK interface.

windmill.note: The documented agent integrations call providers, scripts and MCP tools; interoperable A2A discovery and task lifecycle require a separately implemented protocol adapter.

argo.note: HTTP templates and executor plugins provide integration points, not native Agent Card discovery or A2A task semantics; a reusable protocol adapter is required.

features.name: Remote-task reconnect and reconciliation
features.requirement: Persist remote task IDs and reconcile live work after an orchestration restart.
features.importanceRationale: A restart must reconnect to existing remote work rather than blindly duplicate it.

conductor.note: Polling mode persists remote task IDs, deadlines and failure counts; restart resumes polling, and push notifications have a polling backstop.

kestra.note: The A2A proxy returns text without a durable remote-task handle; worker resubmission alone cannot reconnect and reconcile the original remote task.

temporal.note: Durable history, heartbeats and asynchronous Activity completion retain correlation primitives; remote task discovery and reconciliation require a service-specific adapter.

n8n.note: Persisted execution data and Wait callbacks can retain remote identifiers; recovering and reconciling a live remote agent task needs custom workflow logic.

langgraph.note: Checkpoints can retain remote IDs and RemoteGraph can inspect remote state; reconnecting arbitrary A2A tasks after ambiguous dispatch requires a service-specific adapter.

strands.note: A2A integration exposes task communication and configurable server task stores; graph checkpoints alone do not reconnect persisted remote assignments after restart.

windmill.note: Checkpointed dispatch results and durable resume URLs can preserve remote IDs; A2A reconnection, status reconciliation and safe resubmission require a dedicated adapter.

argo.note: Durable node outputs can retain remote IDs and subsequent HTTP tasks can poll them; an adapter must resolve ambiguous dispatch and reconnect semantics.

features.name: Concurrent external side-effect deduplication
features.requirement: Prevent duplicate external actions across concurrent submissions and ambiguous replies.
features.importanceRationale: Concurrent retries and ambiguous replies must not duplicate consequential external actions.

conductor.note: Stable message IDs support correlation, but no native cross-service atomic ledger prevents arbitrary concurrent external effects after ambiguous replies; receiving services must enforce idempotency.

kestra.note: Worker resubmission is at least once. Preventing concurrent duplicate external actions after ambiguous replies requires the receiving service’s idempotency and reconciliation contract.

temporal.note: Workflow-start identity prevents duplicate workflow starts, not duplicate Activity effects. Concurrent external-action deduplication and ambiguous-reply reconciliation require the participating service.

n8n.note: Execution queues and retries do not supply a cross-service atomic action ledger; concurrent external deduplication and ambiguous-reply reconciliation require the receiving service.

langgraph.note: Checkpointed results do not atomically commit external effects. Concurrent deduplication and ambiguous-response reconciliation require provider idempotency or an application-owned protocol.

strands.note: Python offers in-process invocation idempotency tokens; distributed external-effect deduplication and ambiguous-response reconciliation are outside this mechanism. TypeScript lacks those tokens.

windmill.note: Queue coordination and paid debounce keys govern local dispatch, not concurrent external actions or ambiguous remote outcomes; service-level idempotency remains necessary.

argo.note: Concurrency locks and output memoization do not transactionally couple dispatch with external effects; duplicate suppression across ambiguous replies requires the remote operation contract.

features.name: Durable referenced artifact storage
features.requirement: Store artifacts outside transient worker memory and pass retrievable references.
features.importanceRationale: Accepted work and recovery evidence must survive worker and workspace loss.

conductor.note: Configured external payload storage keeps large workflow and task inputs/outputs outside execution records and exposes retrievable storage references.

kestra.note: Internal storage persists task files and exposes URI references for downstream tasks, inspection and retrieval outside transient worker memory.

temporal.note: Durable payloads support references; official External Storage offloads large payloads but remains Public Preview and needs an operator-managed store.

n8n.note: Configured filesystem persistence in regular mode or database storage in queue mode retains binary artifacts by reference; choose storage mode and retention deliberately.

langgraph.note: Persistent stores retain retrievable namespaced records, and graph state can carry artifact references. Binary/object storage and artifact retention contracts need an external storage binding.

strands.note: Storage and ContextOffloader support persistent referenced content in local files or S3; configure durable storage and disable eviction for retained artifacts.

windmill.note: Supported object-storage resources and SDK references persist files beyond workers; direct S3 resources remain free, while integrated workspace storage has Community limits.

argo.note: Configured artifact repositories persist task inputs and outputs outside pods, with retrievable storage references and credential bindings propagated through the workflow.

features.name: Acceptance bound to artifact revision
features.requirement: Accept an exact output revision and invalidate affected acceptance after repair.
features.importanceRationale: Publication must depend on acceptance of the exact current artifact revision.

conductor.note: The native model stores task results and payload references; revision-specific acceptance and repair invalidation require a separate domain model.

kestra.note: Output fields and stored files have no native acceptance-revision lifecycle; invalidating prior acceptance after repair requires a separate application model.

temporal.note: History preserves payloads, but artifact revision acceptance and automatic downstream invalidation are domain concepts without a native implementation.

n8n.note: Execution records and approvals do not natively bind acceptance to artifact revisions or invalidate downstream acceptance after repair.

langgraph.note: Checkpoint revisions identify graph state; they do not supply artifact acceptance records or automatically invalidate approval after a repaired artifact changes.

strands.note: Structured outputs and stored content do not implement revision-bound acceptance or downstream invalidation after repair; that ledger must be supplied.

windmill.note: Asset references and approval steps do not bind acceptance to an immutable artifact revision or automatically invalidate approval after repairs.

argo.note: Artifact references and suspend approvals carry data, but there is no native acceptance ledger that invalidates approvals when an artifact revision changes.

features.name: Expose a factory as A2A
features.requirement: Provide an Agent Card and an A2A task endpoint backed by a factory.
features.importanceRationale: Factory-as-service reuse matters, but a bounded exposure adapter can supply this boundary.

conductor.note: Workflow-backed A2A endpoints expose Agent Cards, task status and artifacts; enabling integration and configuring access control remain deployment requirements.

kestra.note: The A2A plugin is a client; native callable flow exposure uses MCP, so an Agent Card and A2A task server need an adapter.

temporal.note: Workflow and Nexus endpoints do not natively publish A2A Agent Cards or implement A2A task endpoints for arbitrary Workflows.

n8n.note: Webhook and MCP exposure do not supply A2A Agent Cards or task lifecycle endpoints; an A2A server would be additional integration.

langgraph.note: LangSmith Agent Server exposes an Agent Card and A2A endpoint for assistants; that server capability sits outside the open-source runtime baseline.

strands.note: Official A2A servers expose agents and cards; exposing a whole Graph factory requires an agent wrapper and explicit factory-contract mapping.

windmill.note: Flows are exposed through Windmill APIs and MCP tools; these interfaces do not supply an A2A Agent Card and protocol task endpoint.

argo.note: Workflow submission and status APIs do not supply an Agent Card or A2A endpoint; a separate service must translate the protocol.

features.name: Assignment and attempt correlation
features.requirement: Retain logical work identity and separate retry/attempt history.
features.importanceRationale: Attempt correlation is required evidence supporting ownership, acceptance and recovery.

conductor.note: Task references, iteration identity, task execution IDs and retry history distinguish the logical workflow step from its separately recorded attempts.

kestra.note: A task run retains its identity and attempt history; retries create new attempts while replay can create a separately linked execution.

temporal.note: Workflow, Run and Activity identities distinguish logical execution and retries; Activity attempt metadata and retry history support correlation.

n8n.note: Execution IDs, retry links and node execution data provide correlation; stable logical assignments spanning remote attempts require an application data model.

langgraph.note: Execution info exposes thread, run, checkpoint, task and attempt identifiers. Complete retained attempt history and its remote assignment mapping need tracing or application records.

strands.note: Graph node IDs, execution counts and tracing identify executions; stable logical remote assignments and durable separate retry-attempt histories need application correlation.

windmill.note: Flow status retains failed-job UUIDs and retry counts; individual jobs and parent-job links distinguish attempts while preserving their containing workflow identity.

argo.note: Workflow and node identities, retry-node relationships, timestamps and outputs persist separately, retaining logical task context alongside recorded retry attempts.

features.name: Durable run recovery
features.requirement: Resume orchestration progress after worker or orchestrator failure.
features.importanceRationale: The factory must retain authoritative progress across engine and worker failures.

conductor.note: Persisted workflow/task state and at-least-once delivery support recovery after failure; effects inside workers must tolerate repeated delivery.

kestra.note: Persisted execution state and server heartbeats drive failure recovery and job resubmission; workers must tolerate the documented at-least-once behavior.

temporal.note: Event History replay restores Workflow progress after Worker failure; persistence preserves scheduled tasks and completed Activity results across service restarts.

n8n.note: Saved node progress, queued jobs and persisted Wait states support recovery; arbitrary active work and remote effects still need explicit reconciliation.

langgraph.note: A persistent checkpointer with sync durability saves progress before continuing; invocation with the same thread can recover after failure. In-memory and exit-only modes do not provide this guarantee.

strands.note: Configured session managers checkpoint graph progress after nodes and restore it after restart; unfinished work may reexecute, requiring side-effect-safe nodes.

windmill.note: PostgreSQL persists orchestration state; supported Workflow SDK checkpoints resume completed progress. Interrupted task effects still require retry or reconciliation, not instruction-level continuation.

argo.note: Workflow state persists in Kubernetes; replacement controllers resume reconciliation, while configured retries recover failed pods and SQL offloading supports larger node histories.

features.name: Preserve successful work on retry
features.requirement: Retry failed work without repeating recorded successful sibling steps.
features.importanceRationale: Recovery must preserve completed evidence and avoid repeating successful work.

conductor.note: Task retry and failed-work recovery use recorded execution state; already completed sibling work need not be rerun with the failed task.

kestra.note: Task retries and restart target failed work in the existing execution; explicit replay creates a new execution and can reuse prior outputs.

temporal.note: Replay uses recorded completed Activity results; retrying a failed Activity does not re-execute successfully recorded sibling Activities.

n8n.note: Saving execution progress records per-node data and allows resuming after errors; node retries operate on the failed node rather than completed predecessors.

langgraph.note: Pending checkpoint writes retain successful sibling-node outputs when another node in the same superstep fails, so recorded successful work is skipped on recovery.

strands.note: Graph restore retains completed nodes and schedules unfinished work; incomplete TypeScript nested orchestrators restart internally unless separately persisted. Terminal reruns can start fresh.

windmill.note: Step retries target failed work, and Workflow SDK replay reuses recorded successful results; completed sibling work need not execute again.

argo.note: Retry resumes failed workflows without repeating successful nodes by default; memoized resubmission can also reuse recorded successes in a new execution.

features.name: Durable timers and external waits
features.requirement: Persist waits for time, input or an external decision across restart.
features.importanceRationale: Director decisions and remote input requests must survive restarts without losing authority.

conductor.note: WAIT and HUMAN persist time-based or external-signal gates in execution state, permitting later completion through documented APIs or events.

kestra.note: Persisted Pause and Sleep tasks model external decisions or timers; executions can resume later through the UI or API.

temporal.note: Durable timers and Signal or Update handlers persist waiting state without requiring a continuously running Worker process or conversation.

n8n.note: Wait persists longer timers, webhook callbacks and form waits; time waits shorter than 65 seconds remain in-process and lack the same restart durability.

langgraph.note: Checkpointed interrupts survive restart and await external decisions. Persistent time-based wakeups require a scheduler or Agent Server integration beyond the core runtime.

strands.note: Graph interrupts can persist awaiting correlated input across restart; durable timed wakeups and timer dispatch require an external scheduler.

windmill.note: Suspend/resume events and SDK sleep persist waiting state in PostgreSQL without occupying a worker, with configurable approval timeout behavior.

argo.note: Suspend templates persist waiting state until a duration elapses or an authorized resume/input command arrives; controller replacement retains workflow state.

features.name: Explicit unknown remote outcome handling
features.requirement: Represent an uncertain dispatch/action and reconcile before unsafe resubmission.
features.importanceRationale: An uncertain remote effect must remain unknown until reconciled rather than trigger an unsafe retry.

conductor.note: Persisted A2A IDs aid reconnects, but no universal uncertain-action protocol resolves a lost acceptance response before the remote ID is recorded.

kestra.note: Execution state and error routing are available; a native uncertain-action reconciliation protocol for arbitrary remote services is not provided.

temporal.note: History and timeouts preserve evidence, but an explicit uncertain-action reconciliation protocol for arbitrary external effects remains application functionality.

n8n.note: Saved execution state and error branches do not provide a native uncertain-action reconciliation protocol; remote outcome discovery requires service-specific integration.

langgraph.note: Durable state and interrupts can preserve an unknown outcome while a reconciliation node runs; the remote-action uncertainty model and safe resubmission conditions are application-defined.

strands.note: The documented A2A wrapper and graph state do not provide an authoritative uncertain-dispatch ledger that reconciles effects before resubmission.

windmill.note: Job failure and timeout states do not model uncertain remote side effects or enforce reconciliation before resubmission; that protocol belongs in adapters.

argo.note: Native node phases describe engine execution, not an unresolved remote side effect; timeout/error states do not provide a protocol-level unknown-outcome reconciliation ledger.

features.name: Per-step classified retry policies
features.requirement: Retry selected failures with limits and backoff.
features.importanceRationale: Classified retries are essential standard engine mechanics beneath higher-level recovery.

conductor.note: Task definitions configure bounded backoff retries; terminal-error statuses distinguish nonretryable failures from failures eligible for another configured execution attempt.

kestra.note: Bounded constant, exponential and random retry policies are native; selective failure classification depends on the task/plugin or explicitly authored routing.

temporal.note: Activity Retry Policies define attempt limits, intervals, exponential backoff and non-retryable error classifications with SDK failure handling.

n8n.note: Nodes provide Retry On Fail and error outputs; classified backoff policies require explicit routing, waits or integration-specific behavior.

langgraph.note: Per-node RetryPolicy supports exception predicates, maximum attempts, exponential backoff, interval ceilings and jitter.

strands.note: Provider retries expose bounded backoff; hooks implement classified tool retries. Durable, declarative retry policies for arbitrary graph nodes are not provided.

windmill.note: Flow steps support constant retries, exponential backoff, jitter and retry_if error predicates, with explicit exhaustion and error-handler behavior.

argo.note: Per-template retryStrategy supports failure classifications, expressions, limits and backoff, with last-attempt status, exit code and duration available to conditions.

features.name: Execution timeouts and deadlines
features.requirement: Set execution limits and handle exhaustion explicitly.
features.importanceRationale: Every execution needs limits, while the critical decision is how exhaustion is governed.

conductor.note: Task response, task execution and workflow timeouts have configured outcomes; native A2A additionally supports an absolute call deadline.

kestra.note: Runnable task attempt timeouts, overall retry duration and loop duration bounds constrain execution; configured flow handling determines the exhaustion response.

temporal.note: Workflow and Activity timeout types bound total execution, individual attempts and heartbeat gaps; failures can trigger explicit recovery paths.

n8n.note: Workflow timeout settings cancel executions after configured durations; Wait deadlines and node-specific request timeouts bound external interactions where supported.

langgraph.note: Documented 1.2 node policies enforce async-attempt run/idle timeouts and exhaustion handlers. Synchronous nodes and end-to-end durable factory deadlines need additional handling.

strands.note: Both graph SDKs expose execution and node deadlines. TypeScript deadlines are cooperative and do not automatically propagate into nested orchestrators.

windmill.note: Step timeouts interrupt overlong execution within the instance ceiling; failure handlers and conditional routing can explicitly handle timeout outcomes.

argo.note: Workflow and template activeDeadlineSeconds enforce execution deadlines; resulting terminal statuses can drive explicit failure handling and recovery paths.

features.name: Correlated external run commands
features.requirement: Send validated input or decisions to a particular active run.
features.importanceRationale: Correlated commands provide the required interface for authorized supervision and recovery.

conductor.note: Task-update APIs address a particular running task and accept decision outputs; validating domain payloads and decision authority requires additional checks.

kestra.note: Paused executions can receive correlated resume inputs through UI/API; broader command validation and state-dependent authority need additional application policy.

temporal.note: Workflow handles address particular executions; Updates support validation, acceptance tracking and returned results, while Signals provide durable asynchronous input.

n8n.note: Execution-specific resume URLs correlate authenticated decisions, but arbitrary live-run commands and domain validation require dedicated workflow handlers.

langgraph.note: Thread-scoped Command resumptions and interrupt IDs correlate decisions; documented validation loops reject invalid input before the graph proceeds.

strands.note: Interrupt responses carry unique IDs and route to paused nodes; arbitrary live commands, authorization and domain-level input validation need a service interface.

windmill.note: Execution-specific resume/cancel URLs correlate decisions; structured approval forms and identity restrictions are paid, and arbitrary domain command validation requires application checks.

argo.note: CLI and APIs target named workflows and selected nodes, supplying declared intermediate outputs and resuming suspended execution under Kubernetes authorization.

features.name: Parent/child cancellation policies
features.requirement: Define cancellation behavior for nested work and reconcile outcomes.
features.importanceRationale: Cancellation needs explicit outcomes, but its implementation can use engine and service contracts.

conductor.note: Subworkflow termination and explicit remote CANCEL_AGENT provide cancellation primitives; remote outcomes and detached child policies still require reconciliation.

kestra.note: Execution kill supports child propagation control, but completion of cancellation inside opaque remote services remains dependent on their integrations.

temporal.note: Parent Close Policy and SDK cancellation modes control native child workflows. Cancellation acceptance and actual completion inside opaque remote services still require integration and reconciliation.

n8n.note: Executions can be canceled and subworkflows can be awaited; no comprehensive parent-close policy matrix reconciles cancellation of independent remote child work.

langgraph.note: Async execution can be interrupted, and Agent Server supplies run cancellation. Parent/child abandonment policies and reconciliation of remote effects need explicit application logic.

strands.note: Hooks cancel pending nodes and agent signals stop cooperative work; nested and remote cancellation policies with reconciled final outcomes need additional coordination.

windmill.note: Official SDK APIs cancel queued or running jobs and retain reasons; configurable parent-close policies and remote-child outcome reconciliation require additional orchestration.

argo.note: Stop runs exit handlers and terminate skips them; independently created child workflows and opaque remote tasks need explicit cancellation propagation and outcome reconciliation.

features.name: Compensating actions
features.requirement: Run explicit application-defined recovery steps for reversible effects.
features.importanceRationale: Explicit recovery of reversible effects is valuable for factories that perform those effects.

conductor.note: A failureWorkflow can inspect completed actions and execute explicitly authored compensations; application services implement each actual undo operation.

kestra.note: Authored error/finalization tasks and subflows can perform explicit recovery actions; application implementations determine whether those effects are actually reversible.

temporal.note: Documented Saga patterns execute explicit compensating Activities under durable Workflow control; application code supplies each effect-specific compensation.

n8n.note: Authored error outputs and reusable error workflows can execute explicit compensating actions; application logic supplies effect-specific undo steps and their order.

langgraph.note: Documented node error handlers run after retry exhaustion and can route to application-defined compensating steps with Command.

strands.note: Ordinary workflow SDK code can catch failures and invoke compensating tools; application-defined error handlers specify the recovery sequence for reversible effects.

windmill.note: Flow error handlers and durable SDK exception paths can execute explicitly authored compensating actions; application implementations supply the actual undo operations.

argo.note: Exit handlers and result-conditioned recovery templates run application-defined cleanup or reversal steps; authors define which external effects can actually be compensated.

features.name: Concurrency and capacity limits
features.requirement: Bound workflow/task concurrency and queue excess work.
features.importanceRationale: Concurrent production, maintenance and experiments must respect shared resource limits.

conductor.note: Task concurrentExecLimit bounds in-flight tasks across polling workers and leaves excess work queued until capacity is released. This supplies task processing capacity; unified whole-factory admission and remote spending reservations remain separate integration.

kestra.note: Flow concurrency limits queue excess executions, while Parallel/Loop limits bound task expansion; namespace-wide and tenant-wide controls have edition considerations.

temporal.note: Worker slots, concurrency settings and Task Queue dispatch throttling bound processing capacity while excess Workflow and Activity Tasks remain queued.

n8n.note: Production limits and queue-worker concurrency bound processing; manual, subworkflow, error and CLI executions have documented exclusions from regular-mode limits.

langgraph.note: max_concurrency bounds tasks in one graph invocation. Shared run queues, deployment worker capacity and admission across factories require Agent Server or external infrastructure.

strands.note: TypeScript graphs bound local node concurrency and Python workflow tools bound thread pools; distributed admission queues and reserved cross-factory capacity remain external.

windmill.note: Worker pools and per-loop parallelism bound execution; global per-flow/script concurrency keys and admission windows require Cloud or Enterprise.

argo.note: Controller, namespace, workflow and template parallelism plus mutexes/semaphores bound concurrency and queue excess work; shared database locks can coordinate multiple controllers.

features.name: Authoritative attempt ownership
features.requirement: Prevent stale or competing workers from committing the same task result.
features.importanceRationale: Stale or competing attempts must not commit authoritative progress or acceptance.

conductor.note: The engine ignores completion after task timeout. Fencing competing still-active worker deliveries needs release-specific proof; this rating concerns result commitment, not external effects.

kestra.note: Worker job ownership and heartbeat recovery coordinate attempts. The exact rejection of obsolete result commits after reassignment needs verification against a pinned release.

temporal.note: Service-managed Activity task tokens and execution state reject obsolete completion attempts; external side effects still require their own fencing.

n8n.note: Queue and scheduler claims coordinate local ownership. General rejection of obsolete node-result commits after recovery needs verification; remote-effect fencing is a separate contract.

langgraph.note: Timed-out attempts discard buffered writes. Cross-process thread claims and stale-worker fencing are not an OSS checkpointer guarantee; hosted overlap controls address only part of the requirement.

strands.note: Session managers explicitly take no distributed lock; competing processes can overwrite state, so authoritative attempt fencing requires an external ownership mechanism.

windmill.note: Atomic queue claims coordinate Windmill workers; stale remote-attempt fencing and authoritative external result commitment still require the capability adapter contract.

argo.note: Leader election and persisted node/task-result identities coordinate engine ownership; stale external completions need explicit fencing, with end-to-end attempt authorization still unproved.

features.name: Attributed spend and budget admission
features.requirement: Attribute service spend to runs and stop admission at configured budgets.
features.importanceRationale: Autonomous execution and improvement need attributed spend and bounded admission.

conductor.note: Time, turn, token or execution quotas are not an attributed monetary-spend ledger with budget admission across remote services; that capability requires integration.

kestra.note: Time, turn, token or execution quotas are not an attributed monetary-spend ledger with budget admission across remote services; that capability requires integration.

temporal.note: No native cross-service spending ledger or budget admission controller; recording usage in Workflow state would be application functionality.

n8n.note: Node counts and execution quotas do not provide a general per-factory external-agent spending ledger with atomic budget admission.

langgraph.note: LangSmith attributes LLM and custom component cost to traces. Atomic budget admission, in-flight reservations and stopping remote factory spend remain application responsibilities.

strands.note: Per-invocation token caps and telemetry provide useful accounting; caps can overshoot within a turn and do not enforce shared monetary admission budgets.

windmill.note: Agent token counts and chat spend reports do not implement a cross-service monetary ledger with atomic per-factory budget admission.

argo.note: Resource-duration statistics estimate requested compute usage, not attributed model/service spend; native concurrency and deadlines do not implement monetary budget admission.

features.name: API, event and schedule starts
features.requirement: Start executions through calls, events and schedules.
features.importanceRationale: Calls, events and schedules provide operational entry points without defining the architecture.

conductor.note: REST starts, event handlers and the optional native scheduler launch executions; required event-broker and scheduler modules must be configured.

kestra.note: API calls, schedules, webhooks, flow-state changes and plugin event triggers start executions through native supported integration surfaces.

temporal.note: SDK and API clients start Workflows, event handlers can invoke those clients, and native Schedules start recurring executions.

n8n.note: Webhook, application-event and Schedule Trigger nodes start published workflows; APIs and MCP can also invoke eligible workflows directly.

langgraph.note: Core invoke APIs start graphs; HTTP run APIs and recurring cron jobs come from Agent Server, while external event intake requires an integration.

strands.note: Direct SDK calls and A2A servers provide invocation entry points; event subscriptions and scheduled starts belong to deployment infrastructure.

windmill.note: Flows support direct API/MCP calls, webhooks, event integrations and cron schedules; individual event integrations retain their documented deployment requirements.

argo.note: REST/CLI submissions, authenticated event bindings and CronWorkflows start executions; event queue delivery and admission limits require ordinary operational configuration.

features.name: Overlapping-trigger policies
features.requirement: Choose queue, skip or coalesce behavior for overlapping work.
features.importanceRationale: Admission must handle overlapping work, with simple queue or coalesce policies sufficient initially.

conductor.note: The scheduler explicitly lacks an overlap-policy field; a new scheduled run may start while the prior execution remains active.

kestra.note: Trigger concurrency and flow queue/cancel/fail controls exist; current pages disagree on skipped versus queued blocked triggers, so pin and verify behavior.

temporal.note: Schedule overlap policies include skip, buffer-one, buffer-all, allow-all, cancel-other and terminate-other, providing explicit behavior for overlapping scheduled work.

n8n.note: Production concurrency limits queue excess starts, but per-factory skip, coalesce and replacement policies require explicit coordination beyond global FIFO control.

langgraph.note: Agent Server supports enqueue, reject, interrupt and rollback strategies for overlapping thread runs; documentation explicitly excludes these controls from OSS LangGraph.

strands.note: Single-agent concurrency guards reject overlapping invocations; workflow-wide queue, skip and coalesce policies across processes require an admission layer.

windmill.note: Normal jobs queue for workers; shared concurrency limits and debounce/coalescing policies are Cloud or Enterprise features, with explicit grouping keys.

argo.note: Cron concurrency policies allow, forbid or replace overlaps; workflow mutexes and semaphores provide queued admission for shared execution scopes.

features.name: Priority and fair dispatch
features.requirement: Prioritize ready work with documented ordering/fairness controls.
features.importanceRationale: Dispatch fairness becomes more valuable as factories compete; reserved capacity remains required.

conductor.note: Workflow start priority and task-domain capacity lanes prioritize work; end-to-end fairness across competing factories is not established by those controls.

kestra.note: Enterprise worker queues provide reserved-capacity priority lanes; equivalent documented fairness controls are outside the OSS baseline selected for this comparison.

temporal.note: Self-hosted Task Queues support priority levels and configurable weighted fairness; ordering is approximate across queue partitions, not a global strict sequence.

n8n.note: Documented execution queues use FIFO and worker concurrency; configurable business priority and weighted fair dispatch are not native Community controls.

langgraph.note: The reviewed core and deployment controls bound concurrency but do not provide a documented factory task-priority and fair-dispatch contract.

strands.note: The Python workflow tool sorts ready tasks by numeric priority; no distributed fairness policy or equivalent Graph priority scheduler is documented.

windmill.note: Community jobs follow scheduled queue ordering; numeric step priority and advanced worker priority tags require Enterprise, without a general fairness contract.

argo.note: Queued workflows use explicit numeric priority, then creation-time ordering for locks; namespace limits and multi-lock blocking constrain achievable dispatch fairness.

features.name: Continuous work eligibility reconciliation
features.requirement: Continuously reconcile authoritative external ownership and permission changes against active work.
features.importanceRationale: External ownership changes require reconciliation where an external work system governs assignments.

conductor.note: Engine task eligibility follows workflow state; cancellation or reassignment in an external work system needs a dedicated synchronization authority.

kestra.note: Triggers evaluate start conditions, but continuous authority over canceled or reassigned external work items requires a separate reconciliation capability.

temporal.note: Signals, Updates and cancellation accept intervention commands; detecting and continuously reconciling external work ownership and authorization requires an application authority.

n8n.note: Triggers and callbacks can report changes, but the baseline has no native continuous reconciliation of external work ownership, cancellation and current authorization.

langgraph.note: Invocation and interrupts expose control points, but no built-in reconciler tracks changing external work ownership and revokes active factory eligibility.

strands.note: No native reconciler tracks external assignment ownership or permission changes against live factories; tool policies alone do not supply that lifecycle.

windmill.note: Execution permissions and schedule validators do not continuously reconcile external work ownership or revoked eligibility against assignments already active elsewhere.

argo.note: RBAC authorizes API operations and pod identities; the controller does not continuously interpret external assignment ownership or revoke remote work when eligibility changes.

features.name: Missed schedule and catch-up policies
features.requirement: Define what happens to scheduled starts missed during downtime.
features.importanceRationale: Missed schedules can initially use a simple explicit skip or operator-recovery policy.

conductor.note: The scheduler can replay missed cron slots or advance from current time; catch-up bursts require capacity-aware and idempotent downstream services.

kestra.note: Schedule recovery explicitly chooses ALL, LAST or NONE for missed slots, with a maximum accepted lateness option and backfill support.

temporal.note: Schedules define a catchup window, explicit backfill and pause-on-failure behavior, preserving deliberate handling of starts missed during service downtime.

n8n.note: Opt-in durable scheduler from 2.36 provides grace periods and skip or latest-missed catch-up policies; it does not replay every missed occurrence.

langgraph.note: The OSS runtime supplies no scheduler or missed-start policy. Reviewed Agent Server cron documentation does not establish configurable downtime catch-up semantics.

strands.note: The in-process SDK has no native durable schedule service or missed-trigger catch-up policy; scheduling infrastructure must supply these semantics.

windmill.note: Persisted scheduled jobs and skip validators help delayed execution; bounded catch-up windows and replay of missed cron ticks need integration.

argo.note: CronWorkflows configure missed-start grace with startingDeadlineSeconds; automatic recovery schedules one eligible missed instance, with documented backfill patterns for broader catch-up.

features.name: Roles and scoped operation permissions
features.requirement: Control who may author, publish, invoke or operate workflows.
features.importanceRationale: Invocation, repair, authoring and publication need distinct enforceable authority.

conductor.note: OSS REST and A2A are open by default; scoped integrated authentication is enterprise functionality, otherwise an external gateway must enforce access.

kestra.note: Scoped RBAC, service accounts and richer authentication are Enterprise features; OSS basic authentication does not supply equivalent operation-level authorization.

temporal.note: Self-hosted JWT claims and Authorizer plugins enforce API permissions; product-specific author, publisher and operator separation needs configured or custom authorization.

n8n.note: Community has basic owner and creator boundaries plus MCP permissions; shared projects, fine-grained collaboration and advanced governance require paid editions.

langgraph.note: Agent Server offers per-resource authorization handlers outside the OSS runtime. Distinct authoring, publication and recovery roles still require an explicit policy.

strands.note: Cedar authorizes identity-aware tool calls in both SDKs; author, publisher and workflow-operator permissions require a separate control-plane authorization model.

windmill.note: Workspace roles, item/folder permissions and execution identities control authoring, invocation and operation; operators cannot edit or deploy scripts and flows.

argo.note: Kubernetes resource verbs and namespace roles separate template management, workflow submission and operation; optional SSO maps users/groups to scoped service accounts.

features.name: Assignment-scoped context and access
features.requirement: Enforce data/tool access scopes per invocation across remote services.
features.importanceRationale: Opaque services and concurrent factories must preserve assignment-level data and permission boundaries.

conductor.note: Invocation context and credential bindings scope supplied data; enforcing tool and data permissions inside opaque remote agents remains their responsibility.

kestra.note: Selected inputs and Enterprise isolation constrain local execution, but invocation-specific permissions across opaque remote services require service-side enforcement and bindings.

temporal.note: Namespaces, authorization and encrypted payloads provide isolation primitives; per-assignment remote data and tool permissions require service enforcement.

n8n.note: Credential ownership and selected input mapping constrain access locally; per-assignment remote tool scopes and tenant isolation need service-specific enforcement.

langgraph.note: Thread and per-invocation subgraph namespaces isolate context. Enforcing remote tool permissions and data access requires authorization and service boundaries beyond state schemas.

strands.note: Per-context A2A factories, invocation metadata and Cedar tool policies provide isolation primitives; remote services must enforce their own data and credential boundaries.

windmill.note: Community execution identities and separately configured process/container boundaries provide isolation primitives. Public source marks NSJAIL as Enterprise/testing-only, while docs are inconsistent; do not assume free production NSJAIL. Remote assignment scopes still require service enforcement.

argo.note: Namespaces, workflow service accounts and network/storage policies supply isolation primitives; remote capability scopes require adapters, and unrestricted authors can select namespace service accounts.

features.name: Required independent acceptance gates
features.requirement: Enforce acceptance paths and independence guarantees before publication.
features.importanceRationale: Independent acceptance is the central safeguard between generated work and publication.

conductor.note: Native waits and branches enforce configured paths, but reviewer independence and required acceptance policy are application-level constraints requiring validation.

kestra.note: Pause/approval and branching implement review steps; proving independent reviewers and enforcing non-bypassable acceptance across publications needs domain policy.

temporal.note: Durable conditions and decision handlers enforce coded gates, while reviewer independence and globally non-bypassable publication rules require application policy.

n8n.note: Human tool approvals and conditional paths provide gates; independent reviewer identity and non-bypassable factory-wide acceptance policies require additional enforcement.

langgraph.note: Interrupts and conditional transitions enforce coded review paths; reviewer independence and a publication gate that authors cannot bypass need external policy enforcement.

strands.note: Interrupts and conditional edges can gate downstream publication; reviewer independence and non-bypassable publication authority require explicit service and policy design.

windmill.note: Native suspension supplies approval gates; required groups and disabled self-approval are paid, while non-bypassable factory acceptance policy needs additional validation.

argo.note: Dependencies and suspend inputs express approval paths; author restrictions and independent publication authority must additionally prevent bypass and enforce reviewer independence.

features.name: Reject stale approvals
features.requirement: Reject a decision for an artifact or run state that has since changed.
features.importanceRationale: Late approval must never release a changed artifact or superseded run state.

conductor.note: Task completion targets a task ID; artifact-revision comparison and stale approval rejection are not represented by the native human-task contract.

kestra.note: Resume addresses an execution, but the approval contract does not bind acceptance to immutable artifact revisions or automatically reject stale decisions.

temporal.note: Update validators can reject mismatched current state before acceptance; artifact revision checks and decision freshness remain application-specific conditions.

n8n.note: Wait callbacks identify executions and tool approvals bind proposed parameters; the baseline does not bind approvals to artifact revisions or automatically reject obsolete evidence.

langgraph.note: Interrupt IDs and validation loops correlate resumed input. Comparing the approved artifact revision with authoritative current state is an application rule, not a built-in approval guarantee.

strands.note: Interrupt IDs correlate responses but do not reject approvals against changed artifact revisions or superseded business state; revision authority requires application logic.

windmill.note: Resume URLs identify a step or flow, including optional pre-approvals; they do not automatically reject decisions invalidated by changed artifact revisions.

argo.note: Scoped node commands resume a selected wait but do not inherently compare an approval with the current artifact revision or superseded acceptance state.

features.name: Publication policy validation
features.requirement: Check approved identities, permissions, bounds and non-bypassable gates before publishing.
features.importanceRationale: Agent-authored definitions must not bypass approved capabilities, limits or required review.

conductor.note: Structural and runtime schema validation are native; approved service identities, immutable review gates and publication permissions require domain-specific policy checks.

kestra.note: Enterprise policies can validate and enforce flow/plugin configuration; catalog identity, review independence and acceptance invariants still need Exomachina-specific checks.

temporal.note: No native factory publication policy checker validates capability identities, budgets and required review paths before deploying arbitrary Workflow code.

n8n.note: Schema validation and node restrictions provide limited checks; domain policy is custom, while built-in workflow reviews are Enterprise Preview.

langgraph.note: Graph compilation validates structure, not capability allowlists, publication authority, mandatory quality paths or global factory budgets.

strands.note: Graph construction and Cedar schema checks validate structure and tool policy; approved identities, global bounds and mandatory factory acceptance paths need domain checks.

windmill.note: Enterprise protection rulesets restrict direct deployment and route changes through review paths; capability allowlists, bounded graphs and required acceptance paths need domain checks.

argo.note: Strict/Secure template restrictions and structural validation constrain submissions; approved capability identities, bounded domain loops and non-bypassable acceptance paths need additional admission policy.

features.name: Trace-driven engineering improvement
features.requirement: Continuously turn incident evidence and routine execution traces into tested, governed new factory versions; publishing remains separate from proposing or repairing.
features.importanceRationale: Continuous trace-driven engineering is now an explicit required factory responsibility.

conductor.note: Versioning and test APIs support deliberate updates; automatically converting execution feedback into governed factory improvements requires a separate authoring capability.

kestra.note: Authoring skills and revisions facilitate intentional changes; a feedback-driven, tested and governed factory-improvement loop is a separate application capability.

temporal.note: SDK tests and code versioning are available, but converting run feedback into governed factory improvements is not a built-in lifecycle.

n8n.note: MCP authoring, test runs and publication support deliberate changes; converting run feedback into tested, governed factory improvements requires a separate authoring capability.

langgraph.note: LangSmith Engine detects trace issues and proposes code fixes with regression examples. It is a separate platform service; protected evaluation and governed factory publication remain additional policy.

strands.note: Python Evals diagnoses existing traces and evaluates changes; continuously publishing governed factory revisions requires an engineering controller and separate release authority.

windmill.note: AI assistance, CI tests and agent eval comparisons support individual improvements; continuous trace-driven proposal, verification and governed promotion remain an application capability.

argo.note: Execution archives and reusable workflows provide evidence and execution primitives, but no native continuous engineering loop proposes, evaluates and governs improved factory versions.

features.name: Secret references and credential binding
features.requirement: Bind environment credentials without embedding secret values in definitions.
features.importanceRationale: Secure credential binding is mandatory infrastructure and can use existing secret providers.

conductor.note: Credential injection and per-call headers are documented, but verify OSS secret-provider coverage; secure environment binding may live in workers or gateways.

kestra.note: OSS secret() resolves environment-backed references outside flow YAML; dedicated secret storage, fine-grained access control and audit are Enterprise capabilities.

temporal.note: Activities can use environment credentials and payload encryption; there is no built-in factory credential-binding catalog or secret-management service.

n8n.note: Nodes bind encrypted credential records by reference instead of embedding secrets; external vault integration is separately paid and excluded from this baseline.

langgraph.note: Applications and CLI deployment configuration can bind environment credentials; secret storage, rotation and narrowly scoped service credential issuance remain hosting concerns.

strands.note: Model clients support environment-supplied credentials and configured authenticated clients, allowing SDK applications to bind secrets outside graph code and task documents.

windmill.note: Encrypted workspace variables and resources bind credentials at execution; access follows the job identity instead of embedding secret values in flow definitions.

argo.note: Kubernetes Secret references bind environment variables, mounted files and artifact credentials without placing secret values in workflow documents.

features.name: Run history and audit evidence
features.requirement: Inspect outcomes, attempts, errors and operator activity.
features.importanceRationale: Recovery, audit and continuous improvement all depend on durable execution evidence.

conductor.note: Execution and task histories support operational diagnosis; authenticated operator audit evidence needs configured identity and auditing beyond the open OSS API baseline.

kestra.note: Task attempts, errors and execution histories are native; comprehensive authenticated operator audit logs are an Enterprise feature beyond the OSS baseline.

temporal.note: Event History records durable execution decisions, results and failures; Web UI and CLI expose histories and recorded operational commands.

n8n.note: Saved executions show outcomes and errors; complete operator audit streaming and advanced governance are excluded from the free Community baseline.

langgraph.note: Persistent state history records checkpoints and execution errors. Comprehensive operator audit and retained tracing require additional instrumentation or LangSmith.

strands.note: OpenTelemetry captures execution inputs, outputs, errors and metrics; durable queryable run history and operator audit records require configured observability and application storage.

windmill.note: Job history provides execution metadata, errors and results with Community retention limits. Official pricing and audit documentation conflict on free operator audit availability; source/build verification is required before claiming complete retained audit evidence.

argo.note: Workflow status and SQL archives retain outcomes, nodes and attempts; logs need separate retention, and creator labels do not provide a complete operator audit.

features.name: Workflow test harness
features.requirement: Test routing and failures with supplied activity/task results.
features.importanceRationale: Authoring and self-improvement require reproducible proof of routing, faults and acceptance behavior.

conductor.note: The workflow test API supplies task outputs and simulated timing, tests branches and nested workflows, and returns a simulated execution.

kestra.note: The native fixture-and-assertion workflow Unit Tests feature is Enterprise; OSS can execute test flows but lacks that same declarative harness.

temporal.note: Official SDK test environments support Activity substitutes, failure injection, time skipping and historical replay without deploying production Workers.

n8n.note: MCP test_workflow substitutes supplied outputs and executes logic nodes; credential-free I/O still runs, and comprehensive failure simulation needs additional setup.

langgraph.note: Documented tests compile graphs with isolated checkpointers, exercise individual nodes and resume selected sections; ordinary test substitutes can supply node results and failures.

strands.note: Python Evals supports controlled tool failures and simulations; deterministic graph-routing assertions using supplied node results still require SDK test fixtures.

windmill.note: Flow previews accept mocked step outputs and execute routing before deployment; CI test scripts provide assertions and regression status for scripts and flows.

argo.note: Lint checks definitions and memoization reuses outputs, but the assessed authoring tools provide no workflow test harness for scripted task-result and failure injection.

features.name: Executable graph and live run view
features.requirement: Inspect the declared graph and actual branch/step status.
features.importanceRationale: A live graph helps operators understand execution, but does not supply execution guarantees.

conductor.note: The stored executable definition has UI parity, and execution inspection exposes actual task states alongside the workflow graph structure.

kestra.note: The UI presents executable flow structure and execution state, including topology, task status, logs and outputs for inspection.

temporal.note: The Web UI shows histories, timelines and execution state, but arbitrary SDK control flow has no native declared executable factory graph view.

n8n.note: The executable node canvas shows manual progress and data; saved production executions expose the executed graph and node results.

langgraph.note: The SDK renders graph structure; LangSmith Studio adds interactive graph execution and state views outside the OSS runtime baseline.

strands.note: SDK topology, node status and progress events are available programmatically; a built-in visual factory graph and live execution console are not supplied.

windmill.note: The flow editor displays executable modules and live step status; preview and run views expose per-step logs, outputs and iteration details.

argo.note: The workflow UI displays declared dependencies and live node outcomes, backed by the same persisted workflow resources that drive execution.

features.name: Progress and lifecycle events
features.requirement: Consume execution state and progress updates programmatically.
features.importanceRationale: Programmatic observations connect supervision and maintenance to authoritative execution state.

conductor.note: The PostgreSQL-only source variant retains explicit EVENT tasks and execution APIs, but removes the workflow-event-listener module that publishes automatic lifecycle status to Kafka, queues or webhooks. Add a separate publisher for equivalent automatic events.

kestra.note: Execution APIs and flow-state triggers expose lifecycle transitions; plugin triggers and outputs supply programmatic progress integration for configured systems.

temporal.note: History APIs, CLI following, Queries and SDK observability expose lifecycle and progress; application-specific progress is published through declared handlers.

n8n.note: APIs and MCP expose execution status for polling; comprehensive lifecycle log streaming is paid, and custom progress requires authored output.

langgraph.note: Streaming exposes state updates, values, task/debug information, custom progress and nested-subgraph events through programmatic APIs.

strands.note: Both SDKs expose multi-agent lifecycle hooks and streaming node events, allowing applications to consume progress, completions, interrupts and failures programmatically.

windmill.note: Official job APIs expose lifecycle status, logs and results; SDK progress setters/getters provide programmatic intermediate observations without requiring a separate telemetry subsystem.

argo.note: API/CLI watches and persisted workflow progress expose lifecycle state programmatically; Kubernetes Events are lossy notifications and must not be treated as durable automation history.

features.name: Goals, accountable owners and escalation
features.requirement: Manage purpose and decision authority above individual executions.
features.importanceRationale: Accountable goals and escalation remain required domain capabilities above the engine.

conductor.note: Workflow metadata and decision gates do not provide a goal/owner work-management layer spanning executions; Exomachina must supply that domain capability.

kestra.note: Enterprise Cases add incident ownership, response targets and remediation tracking; general factory goals and authority across executions remain application-level concepts.

temporal.note: Workflow identities and search metadata do not provide a native goal, accountable-owner and escalation work-management layer above executions.

n8n.note: Workflow owners, tags and execution lists do not constitute a native accountable-goal and escalation layer above individual factory runs.

langgraph.note: Thread and run management do not provide factory goals, accountable supervisors, external work ownership or escalation policy as a native domain model.

strands.note: Agent goals and workflow tasks do not constitute an accountable work-management layer with persistent owners, decision authority and escalation cases.

windmill.note: Job ownership, failure handlers and critical alerts operate on executions; a goal-level model of accountable owners, decisions and escalation remains separate.

argo.note: Workflow metadata and creator labels describe executions; accountable goals, assignment ownership and escalation authority above runs require a separate work-management model.

features.name: Pinned examples and partial visual tests
features.requirement: Substitute saved step output to test downstream behavior interactively.
features.importanceRationale: Interactive pinned examples are useful convenience beyond an adequate automated test harness.

conductor.note: Mock-output tests substitute results by task reference and iteration; a persistent interactive pin-and-run visual workflow is not the documented interface.

kestra.note: OSS Playground reuses earlier outputs while rerunning downstream tasks, but requires upstream execution; supplied fixture substitution is a separate Enterprise testing feature.

temporal.note: SDK test doubles and replay exist, but there is no native visual canvas with pinned per-step examples and interactive partial tests.

n8n.note: Pinned node outputs and Execute Step support interactive downstream tests; production ignores pins, and past-run Debug in editor requires free registration.

langgraph.note: State updates and checkpoint forks permit downstream experiments; Studio adds interactive state editing, but that visual surface is outside the OSS baseline.

strands.note: Evaluation result caching exists, but the SDK has no visual node-pinning interface or interactive downstream graph execution using saved node outputs.

windmill.note: The editor pins previous successful step results or supplies mocked values, allowing downstream testing without re-executing the original work.

argo.note: Debug pause inspects live containers, and memoization reuses outputs; these are not an interactive visual facility for substituting pinned downstream test examples.

features.name: Historical replay or experimental fork
features.requirement: Restart/fork from earlier execution state with documented side-effect semantics.
features.importanceRationale: Historical forks aid investigation but isolated fresh candidate runs can support initial evaluation.

conductor.note: Retry, restart and task rerun use recorded definitions; explicit restart on latest is supported and can repeat external side effects.
