kestra.note: Replay starts a new execution from a selected task and links the original; prior outputs may be reused, so inspect side-effect boundaries.

temporal.note: Workflow reset starts a new run from a selected history point; later Activities may execute again and require side-effect safeguards.

n8n.note: Past execution data can be loaded into the editor and retried with original or current definitions; this is not arbitrary checkpoint branching.

langgraph.note: Checkpoint IDs support replay and update_state creates a new branch. Nodes after the fork execute again, including external side effects unless separately guarded.

strands.note: Agent snapshots support historical restore and conversation branching; graph history forks and external-effect semantics are not automatically supplied by snapshot restoration.

windmill.note: Editor previews restart from selected steps, branches or iterations; restarting deployed flow executions is Cloud/Enterprise, and rerun external effects need application care.

argo.note: Resubmit creates a new workflow, optionally reusing successful nodes with memoized execution; retries can target nodes, while rerun tasks may repeat external effects.

features.name: Conversational run supervision
features.requirement: Steer a live run through a conversation linked to authoritative run commands.
features.importanceRationale: Conversational supervision can follow reliable authorized commands and ordinary operator views.

conductor.note: A2A input-required continuation can resume waiting workflows through messages; broader conversational supervision and command authorization require an application interface.

kestra.note: MCP flow invocation and paused-run resume inputs provide useful primitives; a conversation continuously supervising authoritative run commands requires an application layer.

temporal.note: Signals, Updates and Queries supply authoritative supervision commands; a conversational interface and its intent-to-command authorization remain application integration.

n8n.note: Chat nodes and human-review channels support conversations and resumed waits; general live-run steering requires an explicit command and authorization design.

langgraph.note: Message state and interrupt resumptions support conversational steering; Studio offers chat mode, while authorized command interpretation and factory supervision semantics are application-defined.

strands.note: A2A input-required tasks and graph interrupts support conversational interaction; translating conversation into authorized run operations remains application-owned.

windmill.note: Flow-as-chat persists conversations but starts a flow per turn; beta AI sessions operate workspace APIs, while authoritative supervision of existing runs needs integration.

argo.note: The native supervision surface is UI/CLI/API commands; conversation identity and authorized interpretation into run commands require a separate product integration.

features.name: Authorized recovery playbooks
features.requirement: Invoke approved, versioned recovery playbooks with scoped repair authority, preconditions, post-repair verification and escalation; repair permission does not grant edit or publication permission.
features.importanceRationale: Self-healing must use bounded authorized actions with verified outcomes and escalation.

conductor.note: Failure workflows and guarded tool execution support repair paths; approved playbook contracts, repair-specific authority and post-repair verification need application integration.

kestra.note: Error handlers and Enterprise Case actions invoke repair flows; scoped operational permissions exist commercially, while playbook preconditions and verification remain authored logic.

temporal.note: Durable recovery workflows, compensation and API authorization provide primitives; approved repair contracts, narrow action privileges and outcome verification require application policy.

n8n.note: Reusable error workflows support recovery actions; approved repair scope, separate edit/publish authority and verified completion require application policy and appropriate permissions.

langgraph.note: Reusable subgraphs and recovery routing can execute approved repair steps; version pinning, scoped repair authority and mandatory verification need application policy.

strands.note: Reusable SDK workflows lack a native versioned recovery-playbook registry with scoped repair authority, verified postconditions and independent publication permissions.

windmill.note: Reusable error/recovery flows and operator permissions support bounded repair entry points; approved playbook contracts, repair scope and verified outcomes require application policy.

argo.note: Reusable templates, scoped RBAC and exit handlers can execute repair playbooks; version immutability, preconditions, verification and distinct repair/publication authority need domain policy.

features.name: Protected evaluation and mutation boundary
features.requirement: Confine an engineering candidate to declared editable resources; protect evaluator code, test data, scoring rules and acceptance policy from candidate modification.
features.importanceRationale: An improving factory must be unable to weaken its own evaluation or acceptance criteria.

conductor.note: Tool and command allowlists constrain supported agents; immutable evaluator assets and candidate workspace permissions require separately enforced storage and execution boundaries.

kestra.note: Enterprise worker isolation and governance restrict runtime access; separating immutable evaluator assets from editable candidate resources still requires deliberate deployment and permission design.

temporal.note: Separate worker pools and configured API authorization provide boundaries; repository, evaluator and dataset mutation permissions must be enforced outside Workflow code.

n8n.note: External Code-node runners support container isolation and read-only filesystems; protecting evaluator definitions and data from candidate-authoring permissions needs additional separation.

langgraph.note: Separate evaluation datasets and resource authorization provide building blocks in LangSmith; confining candidate code and preventing evaluator/test modification require deployment isolation.

strands.note: Docker/SSH sandboxes and tool allowlists can constrain candidate execution; protected evaluator mounts, immutable data and mutation permissions require deployment configuration.

windmill.note: Optional NSJAIL boundaries and separate dataset/scorer permissions restrict candidate access; immutable evaluation policy across external services still requires explicit deployment design.

argo.note: Kubernetes RBAC and restricted templates can isolate evaluator resources; approved publication and namespace/storage policy must keep candidate authors from mutating protected evaluation assets.

features.name: Baseline versus candidate evidence
features.requirement: Evaluate baseline and candidate against the same pinned evaluator and fixtures; retain quality, cost and latency comparisons, uncertainty and an explicit keep/reject rationale.
features.importanceRationale: Changes require comparable baseline evidence rather than a self-reported improvement claim.

conductor.note: Agent eval suites provide trace assertions and optional model judges; paired factory baselines, pinned fixture provenance and promotion rationale require integration.

kestra.note: Enterprise unit tests provide fixtures and assertions, but no native paired quality/cost comparison with uncertainty and keep/reject evidence is established by this test interface.

temporal.note: SDK tests and history replay check workflow behavior and compatibility; they do not implement paired quality/cost experiments or evidence-based keep/reject evaluation.

n8n.note: Metric evaluations compare dataset runs; Registered Community covers one workflow. Immutable evaluator/fixture binding and governed keep/reject evidence require additional integration.

langgraph.note: LangSmith compares experiments on shared datasets with feedback and performance metrics. Pinned evaluator integrity, uncertainty and an authoritative keep/reject decision need additional controls.

strands.note: Python Evals reuses serialized cases and evaluators across implementations; pinned comparison policy, cost/latency tradeoffs, uncertainty and keep/reject decisions require application logic.

windmill.note: Beta reusable-agent evals compare immutable runs, cases and versioned scorers; whole-factory trials, uncertainty policy and governed keep/reject decisions need integration.

argo.note: Parallel DAGs and retained outputs can run experiments, but no native paired evaluator tracks comparable quality, cost, uncertainty and keep/reject decisions.

features.name: Cohort rollout and explicit rollback
features.requirement: Route a bounded cohort of new runs to a candidate, preserve existing run bindings, and explicitly restore a known-good version while recording rollout outcomes.
features.importanceRationale: Improvement needs controlled new-run admission and a verified route back to a known-good version.

conductor.note: Versioned workflow definitions preserve execution bindings; selecting candidate cohorts and restoring traffic to a previous version requires caller-side release routing.

kestra.note: Enterprise Promote copies published revisions between environments with review and audit; cohort routing and coordinated rollback remain external release-process responsibilities.

temporal.note: Full for native Worker Deployments: percentage ramping, pinned executions and explicit rollback. Retain prior workers; quality decisions and arbitrary remote-agent routing remain application responsibilities.

n8n.note: Published versions and paid source-control environments support controlled releases; bounded traffic cohorts and coordinated rollback of their routing require external integration.

langgraph.note: Assistant configurations support version rollback and application state can route behavioral versions. Bounded cohort admission and immutable active code bindings require separate deployment policy.

strands.note: No native factory version router, bounded new-run cohort release or audited rollback controller exists in the SDK; deployment infrastructure must provide them.

windmill.note: Version histories restore earlier definitions and SDK executions remain pinned; percentage cohorts and coordinated traffic rollback require external release routing.

argo.note: Version-named templates and scoped submission support controlled candidates, but cohort routing, rollback records and immutable dependency enforcement require a publication/admission layer.

features.name: Production and evaluation resource separation
features.requirement: Run engineering experiments in separate worker/resource pools and credential/data scopes, with reserved production capacity and no implicit permission to mutate production.
features.importanceRationale: All evaluation must protect production capacity, credentials and effects even with research disabled.

conductor.note: Isolation groups separate HTTP/Kafka queues and thread pools; execution namespaces separate executors, while research credentials and reserved production capacity need deployment controls.

kestra.note: Enterprise worker groups and worker isolation provide dedicated execution boundaries; separating production credentials, quotas and experiment permissions requires configured deployment policy.

temporal.note: Task queues route separate worker pools and authorization scopes namespace access; resource reservations, external credentials and production/research infrastructure isolation remain deployment responsibilities.

n8n.note: External task runners isolate code, but queue workers share execution infrastructure; reserved production capacity and separate experiment credentials require independently configured deployments.

langgraph.note: Separate deployments and credentials can separate production and evaluation. Reserved capacity and restrictions on experimental effects are infrastructure and authorization configuration beyond the SDK.

strands.note: Sandbox backends and separate credential configurations support isolated evaluation; worker-pool reservation and production capacity guarantees require external infrastructure.

windmill.note: Community worker tags and independently isolated hosts can separate execution pools. Production NSJAIL entitlement is unresolved; reserved capacity, protected evaluator assets and credential boundaries need explicit infrastructure and permission configuration.

argo.note: Separate namespaces, service accounts, pod scheduling and concurrency pools can isolate evaluation; reserved production capacity and storage/remote credential boundaries need enforced cluster policy.

features.name: Correlated incident cases across runs
features.requirement: Coalesce concurrent symptoms by incident fingerprint into one owned case, preserving affected runs, diagnosis, recovery attempts and resolution evidence.
features.importanceRationale: Shared incident ownership is required maintenance integration, usually supplied above engine primitives.

conductor.note: Correlation IDs and failure workflows identify related executions; they do not supply a shared incident-case lifecycle or atomic symptom coalescing.

kestra.note: Enterprise Cases link related failed executions and track resolution; documented matching is non-atomic, so concurrent failures can still create duplicate cases.

temporal.note: Workflow identity and event histories track executions; a cross-run incident-case model with symptom fingerprints, accountable ownership and resolution requires an application.

n8n.note: Error workflows receive failure and retry context; they do not provide a shared incident lifecycle or concurrency-safe symptom-to-case coalescing.

langgraph.note: Separate LangSmith Engine groups recurring trace issues and retains evidence. Atomic case ownership, coalesced recovery attempts and maintenance resolution authority need additional machinery.

strands.note: Python Evals deduplicates diagnostic recommendations within results, but does not atomically coalesce cross-run incidents into durably owned operational cases.

windmill.note: Failed-job resolution and alerts describe execution incidents; they do not provide atomic cross-run symptom coalescing into one shared owned incident case.

argo.note: Workflow archives and notifications record run failures, but there is no native cross-run incident fingerprint, concurrent case coalescing or case-ownership lifecycle.

features.name: Production traces become regression evidence
features.requirement: Capture sanitized incident or routine-run examples as reusable regression fixtures linked to their source trace, factory/contract revision and expected outcome.
features.importanceRationale: Trace-derived fixtures strengthen improvement and can grow from an initial curated regression suite.

conductor.note: Agent SDK record/replay and eval assertions reuse sanitized traces; a revision-linked fixture catalog and opaque A2A boundary evidence remain application responsibilities.

kestra.note: Execution replay supplies historical context and Enterprise unit tests accept fixtures; sanitization, trace-to-fixture promotion and revision-linked evidence need integration.

temporal.note: SDK replay tests reuse execution histories to detect incompatible workflow changes; sanitized semantic fixtures and external-agent outcome assertions require separate engineering evidence.

n8n.note: Saved execution debugging and evaluation datasets reuse production examples; Registered Community enables debugging, while sanitization and immutable trace/revision linkage require integration.

langgraph.note: LangSmith can turn trace evidence into versioned dataset examples. Sanitization, factory/contract revision binding and authoritative expected outcomes remain publication checks.

strands.note: Python Evals ingests production traces and serializes cases and reports; sanitization, expected outcomes and factory/contract revision links require fixture governance.

windmill.note: Saved inputs and pinned historical step results reuse production examples; sanitization and a durable trace-to-fixture catalog tied to contract revisions require integration.

argo.note: Archived runs and memoized resubmission preserve source examples; sanitization, revision-linked expected outcomes and conversion into reusable regression fixtures require an engineering integration.

features.name: Rejected-change history and scoped lessons
features.requirement: Retain rejected changes and validated lessons with reasons, source evidence and applicable factory, capability-contract and policy revisions.
features.importanceRationale: Retained rejection evidence reduces repeated mistakes while a simple scoped record can suffice initially.

conductor.note: Persisted agent state is execution memory; contract-scoped procedural lessons, rejected-change reasons and obsolete-guidance invalidation require a separate domain model.

kestra.note: Flow revisions and key-value storage retain data; they do not model validated state-local guidance, rejected edits or contract-aware lesson invalidation.

temporal.note: Durable histories and Workflow state retain execution facts; reusable procedural lessons with applicability, rejected-change evidence and invalidation need a separate application model.

n8n.note: Execution records and memory/storage nodes retain data; contract-scoped procedural guidance, rejected-edit reasoning and obsolete-lesson invalidation are not native workflow semantics.

langgraph.note: Namespaced stores retain arbitrary records, but rejected-change ledgers, evidence-backed lesson applicability and contract/policy revision invalidation are not native factory semantics.

strands.note: Persistent memory and serialized evaluation reports retain useful evidence; rejected-change records and revision-scoped lesson applicability need an explicit domain schema.

windmill.note: Conversation memory, versions and evaluation history retain data; rejected-change applicability, evidence-based lessons and obsolete-guidance invalidation are not native domain semantics.

argo.note: Archived workflow records are execution evidence, not a version-aware store of rejected changes, validated lessons and their contract/policy applicability.

features.name: Opt-in bounded research campaigns
features.requirement: Run explicitly enabled hypothesis-driven experiments without an incident, with fixed objectives, allowed edits, trial and campaign limits, stop rules and a durable keep/reject ledger.
features.importanceRationale: Proactive experiments are a valuable optional extension after required recovery and engineering work.

conductor.note: Documented bounded agent loops and evals are building blocks; they do not implement an opt-in experiment campaign, trial ledger or promotion lifecycle.

kestra.note: Flows, schedules and agent tasks orchestrate work, but an objective-bound experiment campaign with trial decisions and autonomous stop policy requires application implementation.

temporal.note: Durable workflows can host a research implementation, but campaign hypotheses, mutation scopes, experiment decisions and independent trial/total stop rules are application features.

n8n.note: AI evaluation and workflow loops do not supply a hypothesis-driven campaign controller with allowed mutations, trial decisions and independent campaign stop rules.

langgraph.note: Graphs and evaluation tools can be assembled into experiments, but no native opt-in campaign component owns objectives, editable resources, combined limits and the keep/reject ledger.

strands.note: Python Evals provides experiments and stored reports; opt-in hypothesis campaigns, editable-surface limits, shared budgets and durable keep/reject control require orchestration.

windmill.note: Agent loops and beta evals do not implement opt-in hypothesis campaigns with approved mutation scopes, independent trial/campaign budgets and decision ledgers.

argo.note: Schedules, loops and deadlines can execute trials, but no native research campaign model enforces hypothesis scope, spend, allowed edits and a keep/reject ledger.
